items.title: Cross-device conversation sync becomes stale; stale client can hide newer mobile continuation

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

Cross-device conversation synchronization can become stale between the ChatGPT iPhone app and Windows/web.

In the failure state, the iPhone continues to receive and send new messages, while the same conversation on Windows/web remains frozen at an older revision. Refreshing the Windows/web client may eventually catch up, but sometimes only after repeated refreshes or a delay.

The more serious failure occurs when the user continues the conversation from the stale Windows/web state: the newer mobile continuation may disappear from the visible conversation, or the two clients can show divergent conversation histories.

This is not just a cosmetic refresh delay. It appears to be a stale-client / conversation-version conflict problem.

---

## Feedback reference

Feedback ID:

`no-active-thread-01a0dec2-9d2c-7350-be15-e34062f9bf82`

---

## Environment

- Account: same ChatGPT account on both devices
- Mobile client: ChatGPT iPhone app
- Desktop client: Windows/web
- Same conversation open on both devices
- Reproducible repeatedly
- Observed date: September 26, 2026

---

## Observed behavior

### 1. Mobile advances, desktop stays behind

The iPhone app continues to show newly sent messages and newly received assistant replies.

At the same time, Windows/web can remain on an older conversation state and does not automatically advance to the latest server-side history.

The stale desktop tab still appears usable, even though newer messages already exist on the same conversation from the mobile device.

### 2. Manual refresh is unreliable

Refreshing/reopening the desktop client sometimes causes the missing messages to appear, but:

- it is not immediate,
- it may take repeated refreshes,
- there is no visible indication that the client is stale,
- there is no explicit “refresh conversation from server” action.

This means the user cannot reliably tell whether the desktop is showing the latest authoritative conversation revision.

### 3. Stale desktop can continue from an old revision

If the user sends a new message from the stale Windows/web state before it catches up, the conversation can diverge.

The newer mobile continuation may then disappear from the visible conversation or become hidden by the continuation created from the stale desktop state.

This creates a data-integrity concern from the user's perspective: a valid conversation continuation appears to have been lost even though it had already existed on another client.

### 4. No conflict warning

The desktop client currently provides no warning similar to:

- “This conversation changed on another device.”
- “You are viewing an older revision.”
- “Refresh before continuing.”
- “Conversation conflict detected.”

The send box remains active, allowing a message to be sent from an outdated local state.

---

## Reproduction steps

1. Sign in to the same ChatGPT account on iPhone and Windows/web.
2. Open the exact same conversation on both devices.
3. Send a message from one device and continue the conversation on iPhone.
4. Confirm that iPhone shows the newest messages/replies.
5. Return to Windows/web.
6. Observe that Windows/web can remain frozen at an older message.
7. Wait or refresh.
8. In some cases, the newer messages still do not appear immediately.
9. Before desktop catches up, send another message from the stale Windows/web state.
10. Compare the conversation on both devices.
11. The newer mobile continuation may disappear from the visible history or the two clients may show inconsistent conversation states.

---

## Concrete test performed

During testing, short messages such as:

- `pc test`
- repeated `pc test` messages
- `SYNC-TEST-3`

were used specifically to make it obvious which client had received the latest server-side continuation.

The tests showed that one client could be visibly behind even while the other client had already advanced.

---

## Screenshot evidence already captured

The following screenshots were captured during the failure and show the problem from the user's side.

### Screenshot A — Windows/web stale conversation state

Shows the desktop/web conversation still sitting on the two “pc test” messages and corresponding assistant replies while cross-device testing was being performed.

What it demonstrates:

- the desktop UI can remain on an older visible revision,
- the conversation remains interactable,
- there is no warning that the view may be stale.

### Screenshot B — repeated sync failure after prior catch-up

Shows that even after the conversation temporarily synchronized, it later stopped updating again.

What it demonstrates:

- this is not a single one-off load failure,
- synchronization can regress after appearing to recover,
- reopening/refreshing is not a dependable permanent fix.

### Screenshot C — no available update / no obvious recovery control

Shows the client state while attempting to resolve the problem, with no clear client-side update or manual conversation-sync mechanism available.

What it demonstrates:

- the user has no direct recovery action specific to conversation synchronization,
- troubleshooting currently depends on refresh/reopen behavior.

### Screenshot D — explicit sync test across devices

Shows the conversation after cross-device test messages were sent.

What it demonstrates:

- different clients can temporarily expose different conversation revisions,
- the issue is visible at the conversation-history level rather than only delayed typing/rendering.

### Screenshot E — request for manual sync control

Shows the user explicitly requesting a manual “Sync conversation” action after repeated stale states.

What it demonstrates:

- automatic recovery is insufficient for this failure mode,
- a manual authoritative-server refresh would provide an immediate recovery path.

---

## Expected behavior

A conversation should have a clearly authoritative server-side revision.

Before a client sends a new message, it should verify that the local conversation revision is current.

If the server has a newer revision, the client should either:

1. automatically fetch and merge the latest state before sending, or
2. block the send and inform the user that the conversation changed on another device.

A stale client should never silently create a continuation that causes a newer continuation from another device to disappear from the visible history.

---

## Suggested implementation safeguards

### 1. Conversation revision / optimistic concurrency check

Each client should track a conversation revision/version identifier.

When sending a new message, include the revision the client believes it is continuing from.

If the server's current revision differs, return a conflict instead of silently accepting a continuation from stale state.

Conceptually:

`client_revision != server_revision -> refresh / conflict flow`

### 2. Manual “Sync conversation” action

Add an explicit UI action such as:

**Sync conversation**
or
**Refresh from server**

This should:

- discard stale local cache for that conversation,
- fetch the authoritative server history,
- refresh visible messages,
- re-establish streaming/subscription state.

### 3. Visible synchronization status

Show a lightweight state indicator:

- Synced
- Syncing
- Out of date
- Conflict detected

This would immediately tell the user whether it is safe to continue from the current client.

### 4. Preserve both branches on conflict

If two devices genuinely create separate continuations from the same earlier revision, preserve both branches.

Do not silently hide one.

The UI could present:

- “Conversation changed on another device”
- “Choose latest branch”
- or a branch/recovery view.

### 5. Server-authoritative refresh on focus/resume

When a conversation tab/app returns to foreground after being inactive, compare the local latest message/revision with the server before allowing continued interaction.

### 6. Realtime subscription health check

If the app relies on a realtime stream/subscription, detect when that subscription becomes stale or disconnected.

A client can otherwise look “online” while no longer receiving conversation updates.

---

## Why this matters

This bug is more serious than ordinary delayed synchronization because the stale client is still allowed to mutate the conversation.

The failure mode is effectively:

1. Device A advances conversation.
2. Device B does not receive that update.
3. Device B still accepts user input.
4. Device B creates a continuation from obsolete state.
5. One continuation may disappear from the user's visible history.

That creates a risk of apparent conversation loss and makes cross-device use unreliable for long-running work.

---

## Requested fix

Please consider implementing all three layers:

1. automatic server-side stale-revision detection,
2. a visible/manual **Sync conversation** control,
3. conflict-safe preservation of divergent continuations.

Even if realtime sync temporarily fails, these safeguards would prevent a stale client from silently continuing from an obsolete conversation state.

items.body:
Fix Mermaid shape, relationship, and state description parsing

## What changed

- Reject unsupported flowchart shapes and Markdown strings so the terminal renderer preserves the source with an unsupported-feature notice instead of misrendering it. Keep ordinary quoted labels containing shape-like punctuation valid.
- Preserve class relationship targets beginning with `o`, such as `A --orange`, instead of consuming the first letter as an aggregation marker.
- Accumulate state aliases and descriptions in source order: use the first as the title and subsequent entries as body rows, preserving state identity and limiting body rows to 16.

## Testing

Add parser regressions for these cases and description limits, update class and state snapshots, and extend TUI snapshots to verify source preservation for unsupported flowchart syntax.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows Settings reports package version **26.924.2738.0** (the About dialog was inaccessible during the hang).

- Product UI: ChatGPT Windows desktop, Chat/Work interface
- Package: `OpenAI.Codex`
- Package family: `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Bundled app-server version reported in the log: `0.158.0-alpha.2.1`

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this public diagnostic report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, x64. App log reports `osRelease=10.0.26200`; Windows edition was not separately verified.

Observed on 2026-09-27 KST (UTC+09:00). The supplied startup log covers approximately 01:18:17–01:18:51 KST / 2026-09-26 16:18:17–16:18:51 UTC.

### What issue are you seeing?

Launching the desktop app left a dark, otherwise blank window with a persistent spinner. The Chat/Work home screen and existing Local work could not be accessed. PC reboot and Windows App Repair did not restore the UI.

**Confirmed recovery on this PC:** after launching with a local debugging port, selecting the actual main page `app://-/index.html` and sending `Page.reload` with `ignoreCache=true` restored the Chat/Work home screen. The protocol response was checked for errors, and the user confirmed recovery with a screenshot.

**Important target distinction:** an earlier diagnostic selected the first `page` target and actually reloaded `detached-window.html`. That did **not** restore the main screen. Both targets had the title `ChatGPT`. Only the subsequent reload explicitly targeting `index.html` restored it.

This is a single-PC observation, not a confirmed root cause or permanent fix. Normal exit/relaunch after recovery has not yet been reported. Whether an update originally triggered the problem is also unconfirmed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed startup sequence in the affected existing profile:

1. Launch the Windows desktop app with an existing signed-in account and Local projects.
2. The app window appears but remains on the dark spinner screen.
3. Rebooting the PC and running Windows App Repair still leave the same symptom.
4. The supplied log reports successful app-server initialization and account lookup, but the home screen does not become available.

A clean profile, another PC, and a minimal independent reproducer have not been tested.

#### Troubleshooting already attempted

- PC reboot: no improvement reported.
- Windows Settings → ChatGPT → Repair: no improvement reported.
- Temporarily rename `config.toml`, then launch: no improvement reported.
- Run a script to rename selected UI cache directories: no improvement reported. The output confirming which cache directories actually existed/changed was not supplied, so this is **not** proof that cache corruption has been ruled out.
- A `Ctrl+Shift+R` instruction was included in troubleshooting, but actual main-window reload through that shortcut was not verified.
- Diagnostic `Page.reload` sent to `detached-window.html`: main UI remained stuck.
- Diagnostic `Page.reload` sent explicitly to `app://-/index.html`, with a successful response checked: **home UI recovered**.

Windows App Reset, deletion of the entire app-data directory, and reinstalling during this diagnostic sequence were not confirmed actions. The recovery command did not delete project files or session directories. No loss of actual work files or sessions was established.

#### Observed recovery procedure — diagnostic record, not a permanent workaround recommendation

The app was activated with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`. The local target list at `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json` contained:

```text
main page:     app://-/index.html
detached page: app://-/detached-window.html?initialRoute=%2Fdetached-window
```

After connecting to the **main page's** debugger WebSocket, the following command was sent:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"Page.reload","params":{"ignoreCache":true}}
```

The response for `id=1` was received and checked for an error. The Chat/Work home screen then appeared, confirmed by the user and a screenshot.

The user was instructed to completely exit the diagnostic app instance and return to normal launch afterward, rather than leave the debugging port enabled. That subsequent launch result is still unknown.

### What is the expected behavior?

Normal launch should reach the Chat/Work UI and existing work without requiring a debugging connection or manually reloading the main renderer.

Please investigate startup completion and provide a supported fix/recovery path that preserves existing conversations, projects, and user data. A temporarily recovered UI should not be treated as evidence that the underlying problem is permanently fixed.

### Additional information

#### What the supplied log establishes

- App-server initialization handshake succeeds, `Codex CLI initialized` is logged, and the connection transitions to `connected`.
- Local project migration reports completion with `projectCount=3`. This is **not** a full data-integrity check.
- `React root render requested` is logged.
- Account lookup reports `authenticatedAccountPresent=true` and `result=succeeded`.
- `codex-home request` is logged. That single entry alone does **not** establish that this request remained pending forever.
- ChatGPT pub/sub opens and subscribes.
- Both primary and detached windows have load/ready events.
- An Artifact Session host Unix-socket warning occurs earlier. Its causal relationship to the spinner is unknown; initialization continues afterward.

The supplied excerpt does not establish a renderer/IPC race, success of every network request, or an `app_start` timeout. These should not be inferred solely from the excerpt.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.22138 (Linux deb)

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What issue are you seeing?

After upgrading the Linux desktop app from 26.901.41600 to 26.924.22138, the sidebar lists all Codex threads, but:
- Clicking **any** existing thread shows only a loading spinner forever.
- Starting a **new** task stays at "Starting your task…" forever.
- ChatGPT (non-Codex) conversations are not affected.

Downgrading to 26.901.41600 with the same `~/.codex` data fixes it immediately, so this is a regression in 26.924.22138.

Renderer console (Sentry breadcrumbs) on every thread click:
```
[IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=thread-stream-following-changed
[IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=query-cache-invalidate
Matched leaf route at location "/" does not have an element or Component...
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install ChatGPT/Codex desktop 26.924.22138 from the deb repo (`persistent.oaistatic.com/codex-app-prod/linux/deb`) on Ubuntu 24.04 (X11), upgrading from 26.901.41600 with existing threads in `~/.codex`.
2. Launch the app. The `legacy_to_paginated_v1` rollout migration runs and completes.
3. Click any existing thread → infinite spinner. Or start a new task → stuck at "Starting your task…".

Also tried, with no effect: full quit and relaunch; clearing the Electron caches (`~/.cache/Codex`, plus the GPU/Dawn caches in `~/.config/Codex`); stopping every other Codex process (VS Code extension 26.917.62051 app-servers, CLI 0.153.4) so the desktop app-server was the only one using `~/.codex`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing threads open and new tasks start, as they did in 26.901.41600.

### Additional information

**Local data is intact.** Every `threads.rollout_path` in `state_5.sqlite` exists. In `thread_history_1.sqlite`, `next_rollout_byte_offset` equals the rollout file size for every thread, and `rollout_migration_skipped_rollouts` is empty.

**The app-server answers some requests but the UI doesn't follow through** (from `logs_2.sqlite`, desktop app-server process):
- `thread/list`, `thread/attachment/list`, `config/read` etc. are received and answered, so the sidebar populates.
- `thread/read` is received only 3–4 times per launch, and never again afterwards despite repeated thread clicks.
- `thread/start`, `thread/resume` and `turn/start` are **never** received, even when submitting a new task.
- No ERROR-level entries related to threads.

On every launch, the first `codex` child process spawned by the app exits within seconds and stays a zombie (`[codex] <defunct>`). A second app-server instance then runs normally.

**Workaround:** `sudo apt install --allow-downgrades ./chatgpt_26.901.41600_amd64.deb && sudo apt-mark hold chatgpt`

Windows 客户端 Chat 模式下，GPT-5.6 Sol High 疑似未正常进行深度分析，回复质量显著低于网页和手机端

Piped child processes launched from a detached Windows process should not allocate a console window.

Set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` by default for `codex-rs/utils/pty` child commands. Preserve it alongside `CREATE_SUSPENDED` when preparing a child for Job Object containment, since Tokio's `creation_flags` replaces existing flags.

## Testing

Add a Windows regression test that runs from a detached process and verifies that children have no console window and retain working piped stdin and stdout, both with and without Job Object containment.

items.title: macOS Desktop: local app-server exit 127 is reported as an organization/network settings failure

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, an existing executable selected by `CODEX_CLI_PATH` exited with code 127 before starting the Codex app-server. Desktop then displayed the blocking "Organization settings could not be loaded" dialog with network, proxy, firewall, and account troubleshooting suggestions. The dialog did not expose the local process failure or the active CLI override, which made the actionable cause difficult to identify.

The immediate cause was a custom local wrapper with an outdated assumption about the bundled CLI location. This report concerns the desktop error message and diagnostics for that failure, not a request to preserve private application-bundle paths.

## Environment

- OS: macOS.
- Desktop version: `26.924.22138` (build `11645`).
- Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`.
- Installed application bundle name: `ChatGPT.app`.
- Bundled CLI version: `0.158.0-alpha.2.1`.
- An executable wrapper was selected through `CODEX_CLI_PATH` in the GUI launch environment.

## Observed incident and verified checks

The blocking organization-settings dialog appeared after an application update. Retry returned to the same failure. The dialog offered Retry, Sign out, and Quit.

Local diagnostic requests independently reproduced the backend failure without deliberately breaking or restarting the working GUI:

| Backend selected | Result for the same initialization/configuration-read sequence |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled CLI invoked directly | `configRequirements/read` succeeded with `requirements: null` |
| Custom wrapper invoked as the backend | Process exited with code `127`; stderr: `Codex proxy could not find the bundled CLI` |

The custom wrapper searched for a now-absent bundle-relative executable, `Contents/Resources/codex`. The installed executable was present at `Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex`.

Inspection of this installed build's startup code showed that the early organization-settings check maps an app-server launch/initialization failure on the path to `configRequirements/read` to the generic dialog. The Sign out path also depends on the same backend being available. That code path explains why Sign out cannot complete when the backend cannot start; the follow-up investigation did not trigger another live GUI sign-out attempt. Quit closes the application.

The examined early-startup path uses an in-memory logging buffer and records the startup failure before the normal application bootstrap. Quitting at this point can discard that buffered diagnostic. This code observation does not establish that every other logging channel is empty.

After updating the local wrapper's path resolution, the same initialization/configuration-read sequence succeeded through the wrapper as well. The application's organization-policy check was not bypassed.

## Expected behavior

Keep the organization-policy check enforced, but distinguish a local backend launch/initialization failure from a network failure or a returned organization policy.

For this case, show an actionable message such as:

> The local Codex backend exited before organization settings could be read (exit code 127). A custom CODEX_CLI_PATH override is active. Check that executable and its dependencies, then retry.

Provide a local diagnostic detail or copyable error containing the selected backend source, exit status, and a bounded stderr excerpt. Persist a sanitized startup diagnostic so quitting the dialog does not remove the useful failure detail. Explain when Sign out cannot complete because the backend is unavailable.

Automatic silent fallback from an explicit custom CLI override is not required by this report. Any recovery path must still perform the normal organization-policy check successfully.

## Suggested minimal reproduction for maintainers

These are proposed controlled reproduction steps, not a second GUI reproduction performed on the reporting user's machine:

1. In an isolated macOS test environment, create an executable backend stub that writes a fixed non-sensitive diagnostic to stderr and exits with status 127.
2. Launch a fresh desktop process with `CODEX_CLI_PATH` set to that existing executable for that process only.
3. Observe the startup dialog, the available local diagnostics, and whether Retry and Sign out communicate the backend failure accurately.
4. Launch a clean process without the override and compare the startup result.

The stub does not need to implement the app-server protocol, because the reported failure happens before protocol initialization. Avoid setting a persistent GUI environment variable on a normal working account for this test.

## Related report

#28474 describes a Windows browser-policy error masking a missing local CLI path. It is relevant as a similar error-classification problem, but its platform, feature, and trigger differ from this macOS startup case. The targeted search did not establish an exact duplicate of this report.

No conversation transcript, personal filesystem path, credentials, or raw log attachment is included.

### What version of the IDE extension are you using?
26.5917.61114, bundling CLI 0.155.0-alpha.16 (windows-x86_64).

### What subscription do you have?
Not specified. Authentication uses ChatGPT tokens.

### Which IDE are you using?
VS Code.

### What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26100, x64.

### What issue are you seeing?
The extension cannot finish startup behind a Zscaler transparent/intercepting proxy with cookie-surrogate authentication enabled. OAuth succeeds (token exchange returns 200 and the auth file is written), but the first post-login account/read fails with workspace routing discovery failed. Startup subsequently times out.

**Regression evidence: 0.154.0 works on the same network; the affected bundled runtime does not.** This is not a general inability to reach inference: authenticated POST /backend-api/codex/responses returns a real API response, while bootstrap GETs are intercepted.

No proxy environment variables are configured. Respect-system-proxy is disabled; enabling it does not resolve the interception.

Redacted extension logs:
~~~text
[error] Request failed conversationId=none durationMs=646 error={"code":-32603,"message":"workspace routing discovery failed"} method=account/read pendingCountAfter=1 priority=interactive
[error] Request failed conversationId=none durationMs=2898 error={"code":-32603,"message":"workspace routing discovery failed"} method=account/read
[info] account_login_completed onboardingEntrypoint=null success=false
[info] client.performance.span name=app_start outcome=failure reason=timeout durationMs=123895.6
~~~

Doctor reports:
~~~text
WARN websocket Responses WebSocket failed; HTTPS fallback may still work
     handshake transport error http 307 Temporary Redirect: Some("")
OK   reachability inference URL ... reachable (HTTP 403)
OK   network no proxy env vars
~~~
An HTTP 403 establishes HTTP reachability, not API usability; that OK diagnostic is misleading in this scenario.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
1. Use a network where Zscaler intercepts GET requests to chatgpt.com and requires browser-based cookie-surrogate authentication.
2. Launch the affected VS Code extension and sign in with ChatGPT.
3. Observe successful OAuth followed by account/read failure and startup timeout.
4. Compare with the older working runtime/extension on the identical network.

Observed request asymmetry (redirect token redacted):
~~~text
GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/me
=> 307 Location: https://gateway.zscloud.net:443/_sm_ccik?_ordtok=<redacted>&_orig_url=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/me

Following redirects with a cookie jar:
=> 403 HTML interstitial, after the surrogate handshake and retry with ?_sm_nck=1

POST https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/me
=> 405 API response, rather than a proxy interstitial
~~~
Authenticated requests show the same GET interception. The POST /me result only demonstrates different handling by the proxy; it is not an inference success claim. Separately, POST /backend-api/codex/responses returns a real API response.

### What is the expected behavior?
A supported recovery path for proxy-intercepted bootstrap discovery, or an actionable startup error identifying the failed discovery request and proxy/authentication interference rather than a generic routing failure followed by a two-minute timeout.

Please investigate the regression relative to 0.154.0. A reachable Responses endpoint alone should not be treated as proof that required workspace routing can safely be skipped.

### Additional information
#### Suspected failure path from the supplied investigation
- BackendClient::get_accounts_check issues a GET through exec_bootstrap_get (backend-client/src/client.rs).
- In app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor/workspace_routing.rs, the discovery error path retries unauthorized (401) errors when recovery remains; the proxy-generated 403 instead becomes DiscoveryFailed. The 646 ms failure is well below the 15 s discovery timeout.
- The routing cache is populated after successful discovery and provides no fallback for this initial failure.
- exec_bootstrap_get's system-proxy fallback handles connect/timeout errors, not completed HTTP 403 responses.

These source-level observations are supplied as diagnostic leads, not a claim of an independently verified fix against current main.

#### Possible improvements
- Detect unexpected HTML/non-JSON bootstrap responses and report likely proxy interference, with sanitized status/redirect diagnostics. This improves diagnosis but does not itself restore connectivity.
- Consider whether HTTP bootstrap failures should be eligible for a different configured outbound route. Merely retrying via the system proxy will not fix this particular setup if both routes traverse the same transparent interception.
- Investigate a routing-safe recovery mechanism rather than blindly bypassing workspace discovery.

#### Workaround
Pin the VS Code extension to the previous working build using the pre-gate runtime (0.154.0), and disable its automatic updates temporarily. Changing a separately installed CLI does not change the extension's bundled executable. The exact previous extension build number is not recorded here.

#### Related changes identified in the investigation
- #45529 — expose selected workspace routing in app-server account reads
- #45812 — workspace routing support for Responses requests
- #46281 — connect app-server workspace discovery to model request routing
- #46562 — system proxy fallback for login/startup requests

GET /backend-api/codex/models also encounters the proxy's 403, but the model catalog has a cached fallback and is non-fatal. The blocking failure described here is account/read.

## Summary
A looping HTML5 background video appears to shift or squeeze horizontally by about 2 pixels at the loop boundary in the Codex desktop app's in-app browser side panel on Windows. The same local page and video do not show this issue in Chrome.

## Reproduction
1. In Codex for Windows, open a local Vite game at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/` in the in-app browser side panel.
2. Let a portrait MP4 background video (`1080x1920`, `muted loop playsInline`, `object-fit: cover`) play through several loops.
3. Watch the background near the loop boundary. It briefly appears to move left or narrow by roughly 2 pixels.
4. Open the same URL in Chrome on the same computer and compare. Chrome playback appears stable.

## Observations
- The video element and poster image have matching, stable DOM rectangles before and after a loop: `x=593`, `y=239.390625`, `width=430`, `height=735.75` CSS pixels in a `1616` pixel wide in-app browser viewport (`devicePixelRatio=1`).
- `video.currentTime` wrapped across the loop while both rectangles remained identical; video was playing and ready, with no browser console errors.
- Replacing the source MP4 with the original asset and loading it under a revisioned URL did not remove the live visual effect.
- The user inspected a screen recording and did not see the shift in that recording, although they can see it during live playback in the Codex side panel.

This suggests a display/compositing issue specific to the in-app browser or its panel rather than a CSS layout movement, but the exact cause is not confirmed.

## Environment
- Codex desktop app on Windows, in-app browser side panel
- Local Vite server, HTML5 video background
- Chrome comparison on the same machine

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT desktop app 26.924.22138; bundled codex-cli/app-server 0.158.0-alpha.2.1.

### What subscription do you have?

Not captured for this reproduction.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple silicon; `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A parent task used the Codex App `create_thread` tool to create a separate, user-visible project task in a managed Git worktree. Creation succeeded: the worktree and child conversation exist, the child completed its opening turn, and `send_message_to_thread` delivered a follow-up when addressed by its canonical thread ID. However, the parent received only `clientThreadId: client-new-thread:<uuid>`; the materialized child was absent from `list_threads` while active. The other thread tools require a canonical `threadId`, and no exposed tool resolves the client ID to it. The parent therefore cannot reliably discover, wait for, or message its own created task after worktree setup.

Direct `read_thread` by the canonical ID succeeds and reports a title, conversation history, worktree cwd, and an empty `preview`. A read-only inspection of the local state DB confirmed `preview = ''` for this child. The child was archived later in the investigation; the initial `list_threads` omission was observed before that archive operation.

This is a successful creation followed by a discovery failure, not a failed worktree setup or a `send_message_to_thread` delivery error.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In a saved local Git project, call `list_projects` and use its returned project ID.
2. From a normal parent task, call `create_thread` with a title, an ordinary text prompt, and:
   ```json
   {"type":"project","projectId":"<saved project ID>","environment":{"type":"worktree"}}
   ```
3. Observe the immediate `{ "clientThreadId": "client-new-thread:<uuid>", "hostId": "local" }` result.
4. Wait for the managed worktree and child task to finish initialization. Do not send a direct user message to the child.
5. Call `list_threads` from the parent while the child is active. The child is omitted.
6. If the canonical thread ID is obtained outside the `create_thread` result, `read_thread(threadId=...)` succeeds, and `send_message_to_thread(threadId=...)` reaches the child.

The affected child in this reproduction was a separate task titled `Worktree-Nachrichtentest`, with thread source `agent_created_thread`. Its first turn is stored as a `create_thread` tool output containing `<codex_delegation>`, rather than a normal user message.

### What is the expected behavior?

After worktree initialization, a successful, named, user-facing task should be discoverable through `list_threads` even if its preview is empty. The parent should also have a supported way to resolve the returned `clientThreadId` to the canonical `threadId` (or receive a completion event with that ID), so it can use `wait_threads`, `read_thread`, and `send_message_to_thread`.

### Additional information

Likely contributing path in bundled app / codex 0.158.0-alpha.2.1: delegated `create_thread` starts the child with `input: []` and a `toolOutput` named `create_thread`. `codex-rs/state/src/extract.rs` populates preview from user messages but not that response item; `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/threads.rs` excludes ordinary active records with `threads.preview = ''`. This explains why direct ID access works while listing fails. A regression test should cover a named, tool-created worktree task with a completed first turn and empty preview, plus the client-ID-to-thread-ID handoff.

In-app feedback/session reference provided by the reporter: `01a0dde8-8322-7392-9c21-d5529d7a85ba`. Diagnostic upload status was not independently verified.

After updating, normal startup repeatedly leaves the Desktop window on Loading indefinitely. Ending only the initial codex.exe backend leaves Desktop running; its automatically restarted backend restores the UI in roughly 3–4 seconds, and existing conversations can send and receive messages. 2. Wait at least 15 seconds and launch via the registered Windows application entry.
3. Observe persistent Loading for more than two minutes.

5. Desktop stays running, launches a replacement backend and loads successfully.
6. Existing conversations work, but another normal exit/relaunch reproduces the failure.

items.title: app-server account/login/start {type: "apiKey"} overwrites the persisted ChatGPT login shared by every Codex surface

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.157.0 and 0.157.1 (standalone installer, Windows 11 x64). The
code path is unchanged on `main`.

## What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT (signed in with `codex login`).

## What issue are you seeing?

When any app-server client sends `account/login/start` with
`{ "type": "apiKey", "apiKey": ... }`, the app-server writes a fresh
API-key-only `auth.json` to the persistent credential store. That replaces the
ChatGPT tokens that the CLI, the background daemon and the desktop app all
share.

One client choosing API-key auth for its own session silently switches every
other Codex surface on the machine from ChatGPT to that API key. Every
surface then bills to the API platform instead of the ChatGPT plan, and all of
them fail at once if the key is invalid or revoked.

Editor integrations built on the app-server protocol hit this path. For
example, `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` implements its `api-key` auth
method as `account/login/start {type: "apiKey"}`, falling back to
`CODEX_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

## Steps to reproduce

Hermetic, using a throwaway `CODEX_HOME` and a synthetic, never-sent ChatGPT
`auth.json`:

1. Seed `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json` with `auth_mode: "chatgpt"` and tokens.
2. Start `codex app-server` with that `CODEX_HOME`, then `initialize`.
3. Send `account/login/start { "type": "apiKey", "apiKey": "sk-dummy" }`.
4. Read `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`.

**Actual:** `auth.json` now has `auth_mode: "apikey"` and no ChatGPT tokens.
**Expected:** the ChatGPT login persisted for other processes is unchanged,
while this session uses the API key (`account/read` reports `apiKey`).

The script we used:
https://github.com/Superintelligent-Group/superintelligent-codex/blob/sig/harness/scripts/e2e-codex-auth-isolation.mjs

Stock 0.157.0 result:
`{"sessionAccount":"apiKey","persistedAuthMode":"apikey","authJsonUnchanged":false}`

## Root cause

`login_api_key_common` in
`app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs` passes the key to
`login_with_api_key(codex_home, api_key, config.cli_auth_credentials_store_mode, ...)`.
That persists `AuthDotJson { auth_mode: ApiKey, tokens: None, ... }` to the
same store the ChatGPT login lives in.

By contrast, `CODEX_API_KEY` is treated as a per-process override:
`load_auth(enable_codex_api_key_env)` checks it before storage and never
persists it. An app-server client's API-key login should behave the same way.

## Proposed fix

In `login_api_key_common`, when the persisted store already holds ChatGPT
tokens, save the API key with `AuthCredentialsStoreMode::Ephemeral`. The
existing precedence in `load_auth` already prefers the ephemeral store, so
that app-server process uses the key and everything else keeps ChatGPT.

We run this as a patch with a regression test
(`login_account_api_key_keeps_persisted_chatgpt_login` in
`app-server/tests/suite/v2/account.rs`). With it, the same script reports
`{"sessionAccount":"apiKey","persistedAuthMode":"chatgpt","authJsonUnchanged":true}`.
Patch:
https://github.com/Superintelligent-Group/superintelligent-codex/commits/sig/0.157.1

An explicit alternative is a `persist: bool` on `LoginApiKeyParams`,
defaulting to false for app-server clients.

## Not the cause of the 2026-09-25 `sk-svcacct` 401 outage

We first suspected this bug in the widespread `Incorrect API key provided:
sk-svcacct...` 401 from 2026-09-25 (#48237), but that was the server-side
outage. This report is only about the local credential overwrite.

items.body:
## Symptom

On macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), ChatGPT desktop `com.openai.codex` 26.924.20706 (11431), several Chat-mode conversations intermittently lose their composer. In some conversations, clicking the voice control restores text input. One existing Chat-mode conversation remains blocked: text can be entered, but Send and voice controls are both disabled even though the previous assistant reply is visibly complete. Screenshot observed 2026-09-26 22:27:42 Asia/Shanghai; user reports onset around 22:25 and continued failure.

## Redacted client evidence

For the same conversation (confirmed by the matching browser chat route and title), desktop logs show:

- An earlier conversation GET returned 429 around 20:53:59 Asia/Shanghai but was followed by a successful refetch at 20:55:35 with `currentNodeApplied=true` and `statusAfter=idle`. A 429 alone is therefore insufficient to explain the persistent failure.
- 21:44:23: conversation refetch started from `idle`.
- 21:45:25: refetch completed with `currentNodeApplied=false`, `statusBefore=idle`, `statusAfter=streaming`.
- 21:45:53: another refetch started with `statusBefore=streaming`.
- 21:46:16: `GET /conversations/{conversation_id}` returned HTTP 429 `Too many requests`; the client logged `Failed to refetch ChatGPT conversation after an update`.
- No later successful refetch or explicit `statusAfter=idle` for that conversation appears in the available desktop log through 23:21 Asia/Shanghai, despite later route/owner-sync events.
- At 23:10, the user navigated from Settings back to the same desktop chat. Send and dictation remained disabled, and the renewed desktop `GET /conversations/{conversation_id}` returned another 429. Three other conversation IDs had produced desktop conversation-read 429s across the available same-day log, including one within the preceding two hours. The Settings round trip is therefore not an effective recovery in this case.
- In the main desktop log between 21:10 and 23:10 local time, 10 explicit 429s occurred: seven authenticated Chat-directory fetches and three conversation GETs across two conversation IDs. The 429s affect desktop reads beyond one chat; the log does not identify the rate-limit scope or a `Retry-After` value.

In Chrome on the same account, the exact same conversation loads; after loading finishes, entering a non-sensitive 7-character test string enables Send and dictation. No message was submitted and the test draft was cleared. This points to a desktop client state recovery fault rather than a permanent inability to send to the conversation on every client. Switching to a different desktop chat and back did not recover the desktop Send or voice controls.

The UI does not log the Send/voice disabled predicates, so this is correlation, not proof that the 429 caused the disabled controls. The 429 was on a conversation **read**, not a message submission. Separate Codex app-server `thread/attachment/list` queue-full events occurred at other times, but causation with this Chat-mode failure is unproven.

Read-only inspection of the signed desktop bundle indicates that conversation-scoped disable/pending state can gate both Send and dictation. Runtime values of those predicates were not captured, so this identifies a plausible shared mechanism rather than the confirmed trigger.

The full Chat page passes its conversation query's loading/error and submit-disabled state into the composer. Static inspection did not reveal an always-available retry for a failed main conversation query on that page; the visible `Try again` implementation found is for a Work-homepage preview. Please verify this behavior in source and runtime before attributing the lock to it.

## Request

Please investigate whether a failed conversation refetch can leave Chat-mode input eligibility stuck in `streaming` or another non-interactive state after a visible reply completes. The expected behavior is to restore Send and voice once the conversation is idle, or surface a recoverable error and retry with appropriate backoff. Please advise which signed desktop build contains a fix and which redacted diagnostics can distinguish the exact desktop disable predicate from a server-side conversation state.

Please also inspect whether overlapping Chat-directory sync and conversation refetch calls need deduplication/backoff to avoid repeated 429s. This is a suggested investigation path, not a proven root cause.

Related public reports: #42583 (Chat composer disappearing), #37518 (desktop Chat read 429s), and #46440 (Codex-mode disabled Send). These are related symptoms, not proof of a shared root cause.

## Acceptance

Verify the affected original conversation after a completed reply, after navigating away and back, and after application restart. Confirm Send and voice remain enabled when appropriate and that successive messages can be submitted. Also verify other affected Chat conversations.


Prepared with AI assistance at the user's request. No chat content, IDs, screenshots, credentials, or full logs are attached.

### Observed behavior
After upgrading from 26.917.71314 to 26.924.22138 on September 26, 2026 at 21:48 local time, existing chats would not open normally and creating/using a new chat was also unresponsive. Restarting the upgraded app multiple times did not resolve the observed failure. The renderer logged the following twice (21:53:59 and 22:07:25 local time):

```text
RequestError: Something went wrong. If this issue persists please contact us through our help center at help.openai.com.
```

The bundled CLI's `doctor` checks reported configured auth, readable state paths, and a consistent installation. These checks do not establish the cause of the desktop failure.

### Recovery observed
At 22:22 the package was downgraded to 26.917.71314. **The user reports that chat functionality recovered immediately after the downgrade, without restarting the app at that point.** The earlier version of this issue incorrectly stated that recovery happened only after a restart; that was my reporting error. The user later restarted the app, and subsequent session metadata reported CLI 0.155.0-alpha.16.4. That metadata confirms the older CLI was running after the later restart, but does not explain the immediate pre-restart recovery. No repeat `RequestError` was seen in the immediate post-downgrade journal window.

### Limitations
The direct recovery after downgrade strengthens the version association, but it is not a controlled A/B reproduction; the newer version has not been retested because the app is currently usable. I did not observe the `invalid paginated history lineage: missing source rollout` error from #44947, so this should not be assumed to share that root cause.

### Expected behavior
Existing chats open and new chats can be created and used after upgrading.

items.body:
## Description

Arabic RTL/BiDi rendering on ChatGPT Web appears to have regressed recently.

Until roughly one week ago, Arabic responses containing English words, numbers, technical terms, and Markdown tables were displayed correctly or significantly better.

Now Arabic responses frequently render with incorrect RTL/LTR ordering and alignment, especially when Arabic is mixed with:

- English words
- Numbers
- Currency values
- Token symbols
- Technical abbreviations
- Bullet lists
- Markdown tables

The issue affects normal assistant responses as well as tables.

## Environment

- Surface: ChatGPT Web (chatgpt.com)
- OS: Windows
- Browser: Google Chrome
- Language: Arabic (RTL)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open ChatGPT Web.
2. Start a conversation in Arabic.
3. Ask for a response containing Arabic text mixed with English terms and numbers.
4. For example, ask for a comparison that contains values such as:
   - DEX
   - Volume 24h
   - $22.3M
   - RHEA
5. Also ask for the same information in a Markdown table.
6. Observe the rendered response.

## Actual behavior

Arabic and LTR fragments are visually reordered or aligned incorrectly.

Examples of the symptoms:

- English text appears in an unexpected position relative to the Arabic sentence.
- Numbers and labels become visually separated from the text they belong to.
- Bullet points and regular paragraphs become difficult to follow.
- Markdown tables are especially difficult to read because cell content mixes RTL and LTR incorrectly.
- The problem can occur even outside tables.

## Expected behavior

Arabic prose should remain RTL while embedded English words, numbers, URLs, technical identifiers, token symbols, and other LTR fragments retain their natural LTR direction without breaking the visual order of the surrounding Arabic text.

Markdown table cells should also preserve correct bidirectional text rendering.

## Regression

This appears to be a recent regression on ChatGPT Web.

The same style of Arabic responses rendered correctly or significantly better until approximately one week ago.

## Related issues

There are existing RTL/BiDi reports for the Codex desktop app, for example:

- #26250 — mixed Arabic/English rendering in Codex
- #33328 — RTL text rendered incorrectly as LTR in the desktop app

This report is specifically about the standard ChatGPT Web conversation interface on **chatgpt.com**, not Codex Desktop.

## Additional information

The problem is reproducible across multiple conversations.

Screenshots showing the incorrect rendering in both normal text and Markdown tables are available and can be attached.

items.title: TUI: Hook systemMessage renders ANSI SGR escapes as literal text instead of styles

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.157.1` (Homebrew, macOS arm64). Confirmed that `rust-v0.157.1` is the latest stable GitHub release when filing.

The source-level reproduction below was run against the unmodified Hook renderer from that release tag. A separate local experimental build was subsequently used to test a possible fix; it is not the baseline for this report.

### What subscription do you have?

Not disclosed. The renderer-level reproduction is offline and does not require an account or model call.

### Which model were you using?

The issue was encountered through the Red Pen plugin. The isolated renderer test does not invoke a model.

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

The original terminal host/version was not captured. The diagnostic environment reports `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`. The offline reproduction checks ratatui lines and the terminal buffer directly rather than depending on a particular emulator.

### What issue are you seeing?

A Hook `systemMessage` containing ANSI SGR styling can display escape fragments such as `[1;36m` and `[0m` in the `↳ Hook ·` message instead of displaying styled text.

This was noticed with Red Pen's colored grammar feedback. Its output already contains SGR sequences. Changing the plugin to use native newlines fixes its legacy padding/layout, but does not provide ANSI-to-style conversion in the Hook renderer.

I have **not** established a last-known-good version or the commit that introduced this behavior, so I am not claiming a confirmed version regression or that ANSI support was removed globally.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Minimal Hook payload, without Red Pen or an LLM dependency:

1. Save the following as `hook-ansi-repro.py`:

```python
import json
import sys

sys.stdin.read()
print(json.dumps({
    "systemMessage": (
        "\x1b[1;92m[100]\x1b[0m "
        "\x1b[31;9mold\x1b[0m \x1b[32mnew\x1b[0m\n"
        "\x1b[33mNative style\nhey!\x1b[0m plain"
    )
}))
```

2. Add a `UserPromptSubmit` command Hook to the existing Hook configuration (merge this entry rather than replacing other hooks):

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [{
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "python3 /absolute/path/to/hook-ansi-repro.py"
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

3. Start the interactive CLI, review/trust this local Hook through the normal flow, and submit a short prompt. Inspect the Hook feedback.

The minimal interactive recipe above is a reduction of the plugin case; the independently executed reproduction was at the renderer boundary: construct a completed `HookCell` with this string as a `HookOutputEntryKind::Warning`, then call `display_lines(80)`. On the stock renderer, concatenated span contents still contain the literal ESC/SGR sequences, and the expected styled-text assertion fails. No network request is involved.

### What is the expected behavior?

Ideally, SGR colors/bold/strikethrough become ratatui styles, with no literal escape fragments. Styles spanning a newline should be preserved, resets should work, and Codex's own prefix/status styling should remain independent.

If Hook messages are intentionally plain-text-only, please clarify that contract and handle escape sequences without showing fragments. Supporting safe SGR styling would allow plugins such as Red Pen to retain their existing feedback presentation.

### Codex doctor report

Selected fields from `doctor --json`, explicitly run using the retained official binary. Personal/configuration details and unrelated checks are omitted. This was a **non-interactive diagnostic subprocess**, whose `NO_COLOR=1` is noted rather than presented as the original terminal's environment. The Hook/terminal checks were also run with `NO_COLOR` unset.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "codexVersion": "0.157.1",
  "overallStatus": "warning",
  "checks": {
    "installation": {
      "status": "ok",
      "summary": "installation looks consistent"
    },
    "runtime.provenance": {
      "status": "ok",
      "summary": "running brew on macos-aarch64",
      "details": {
        "commit": "unknown",
        "install method": "brew (installation paths omitted)",
        "platform": "macos-aarch64",
        "version": "0.157.1"
      }
    },
    "config.load": {
      "status": "ok",
      "summary": "config loaded"
    },
    "terminal.env": {
      "status": "ok",
      "summary": "terminal metadata was detected",
      "details": {
        "COLORTERM": "truecolor",
        "NO_COLOR": "1",
        "TERM": "xterm-256color",
        "stderr is terminal": "false",
        "stdin is terminal": "false",
        "stdout is terminal": "false"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Additional information

**Source observation:** In [`HookCell::output_lines` at rust-v0.157.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.1/codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/hook_cell.rs), the warning's first line becomes a plain span with `first_line.to_string().into()`, and subsequent lines similarly become plain text. Codex already has an [ANSI-to-ratatui parser](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.1/codex-rs/ansi-escape/src/lib.rs), but this path does not call it.

**Local experiment, not an upstream patch submission:** Parsing the complete message into styled lines before adding Hook prefixes made the two new regression tests pass. A combined selection of all Hook-cell and cursor-rendering tests passed **14/14** with `NO_COLOR` unset. Checks cover colors, strikethrough, cross-line styling, resets, blank lines, and rendered buffer cells.

This is scoped validation, not a claim that the full suite is green: the full TUI run had 5,432 passes, 46 failures, and 8 skips. Four color-related failures passed when rerun without the diagnostic environment's `NO_COLOR`; the remaining 42 were version-related snapshot differences between the release tag (`0.157.1`) and expected development-version text (`0.0.0`), including version-dependent notices.

Any supported solution should convert permitted styling to structured styles, not forward arbitrary terminal control sequences to the terminal.

I searched open/closed issues and PRs for Hook/ANSI, `systemMessage`, and Red Pen, plus public Discussions results, and did not find an exact duplicate. [#23031](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/23031) concerns a broader Windows startup/resume terminal problem; this report is specifically about Hook message styling.

22:54 충돌 로그의 PiP chat identifier를 해당 로컬 웹앱 개발 채팅과 대조했습니다. 조회한 작업 기록에는 다음 흐름이 있습니다.
1. Browser Use로 로컬 웹앱 탭 열기.
2. 접근 토큰 입력란에 로컬 테스트 값을 넣고 접속.
3. 예산 입력·배분·저장 등의 화면 검증.
4. 마지막 UI 확인과 같은 도구 호출 안에서 await tab.close() 실행.

이 기록은 관련 세션의 작업 흐름이며, 통제된 최소 재현 실험은 아닙니다. 23:02 종료 직전의 개별 도구 호출은 별도로 조회하지 않았으므로 그 시점에도 동일한 호출이 있었다고 단정하지 않습니다. 다만 23:02 로그에도 같은 채팅과 연결된 PiP 및 Browser Use 탭 정리가 기록됐습니다.

## 반복 발생 기록
2026-09-26 Crashpad 보고 메타데이터의 확인된 시각(KST):
17:50:07, 18:25:00, 18:39:55, 18:53:18, 19:09:24,
19:34:03, 22:20:52, 22:54:41, 23:02:23.

18:25, 18:39, 18:53, 19:09 인접 세션에서도 마지막 로그가 브라우저 탭 정리와 PiP tabID=undefined 처리로 끝났습니다. 모든 보고 파일이 같은 근본 원인이라고 확정하지는 않습니다.

## 비밀번호 저장/등록 형태의 반복 알림
사용자가 직접 확인해 전달한 표시 문자열:
- synthetic-reference-writer-00000000001
- view-test-0--------------------------------

두 번째 문자열은 관련 화면 검증에서 사용한 로컬 테스트 접근 값의 일부 및 하이픈 반복 형태와 유사합니다. 알림 화면을 캡처하지 못했으므로 정확히 동일한 값인지, 어느 입력값을 어떤 방식으로 인식했는지는 확인되지 않았습니다.

확인 요청:
- 테스트용 접근 토큰 입력이 내장 브라우저의 비밀번호 저장 감지를 유발하는지.
- 비밀번호 저장 UI가 표시되거나 대기하는 동안 탭이 제거될 때 문제가 발생하는지.
- 이 알림과 앱 종료가 서로 별개의 문제인지.

알림 전체 문구, 사이트/출처 표시는 미확보입니다. synthetic-reference-writer 문자열은 검색한 당일 앱 로그와 해당 설치 버전 app.asar에서는 발견되지 않았습니다.

## 기타 오류 (원인으로 확정하지 않음)
조회한 로그에는 다음도 있습니다.
- ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
- Conversation state not found
- No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session
- fs/getMetadata: os error 2/3 (파일/경로 없음)

이 오류들이 앱 종료를 일으켰다는 근거는 아직 없습니다.

## 기대 동작
- 자동화된 브라우저 탭을 닫아도 앱과 다른 채팅이 계속 실행돼야 합니다.
- 웹뷰·디버거·PiP 정리가 앱 종료 없이 완료돼야 합니다.
- 비밀번호 등록을 의도하지 않은 테스트 입력에서 반복 저장 알림이 발생하는지 점검이 필요합니다.

## 조사 요청과 한계
Browser Use 탭/웹뷰 제거, debugger listener 해제, 마지막 Browser Use 탭 종료 및 PiP의 undefined 전환 구간을 충돌 보고와 대조해 주세요. 비밀번호 저장 UI가 관련되는지도 확인 부탁드립니다.

분석 가능한 네이티브 .dmp/예외 스택은 검사한 Crashpad reports 폴더에서 확보하지 못했고, sidecar 메타데이터만 확인했습니다. profile.exit_type=Crashed도 관찰됐으나 실행 중 프로필 값이므로 충돌 시각을 입증하는 근거로 단독 사용하지 않았습니다.

원인 확정을 위한 고의적인 재현, 앱 설정 변경, 캐시/대화 삭제는 수행하지 않았습니다. 현재 결론은 반복되는 시간적 연관성이며, 확정된 원인 진단은 아닙니다.

저장된 비밀번호, 인증 토큰 값, 서버 접속 정보, 대화 전문은 포함하지 않았습니다. 위 두 문자열은 사용자가 직접 보고한 알림 표시 증상입니다.

## 추가 사용자 보고: 세 번째 비밀번호 등록/저장 알림 문자열
사용자가 reference-0-------------------------------- 문자열에 대해 비밀번호 등록을 요청하는 형태의 알림이 다시 표시됐다고 보고했습니다.

현재까지 보고된 서로 다른 표시 문자열:
- synthetic-reference-writer-00000000001
- view-test-0--------------------------------
- reference-0--------------------------------

서로 다른 테스트 값처럼 보이는 문자열을 대상으로 알림이 반복되는 현상입니다. 정확한 생성 주체, 전체 알림 문구와 사이트 출처는 아직 확인하지 못했습니다. 이번 보고는 알림 재발이며, 추가 앱 충돌이 확인됐다는 의미는 아닙니다. 실제 비밀번호인지 또는 기존 비밀번호가 변경됐는지 확인된 바도 없습니다. 테스트 접근 값에 대한 비밀번호 저장 감지 가능성을 조사해 주세요.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow, not a controlled minimal reproduction:
1. Run a local web application in a Codex development chat.
2. Open it through in-app Browser Use.
3. Enter a local test access value in the access-token field and perform UI checks.
4. At the end of verification, close the automated tab (the inspected workflow contains await tab.close()).
5. The app unexpectedly exits. In the two latest incidents, the final tab-cleanup log precedes a new Crashpad sidecar timestamp by approximately 0.95–0.96 seconds.

Latest incidents: 2026-09-26 22:54:41 and 23:02:23 KST (UTC+09:00). The 23:02 individual tool call was not separately inspected, so an identical tab.close() call at that time is not asserted. Native exception stack, token usage and context-window usage were not collected. Root cause is not confirmed.

### What is the expected behavior?

Closing a Browser Use tab should clean up the webview, debugger listener and PiP state without terminating the desktop app or interrupting other chats. Please also investigate repeated password-save prompts for local test/access-token inputs, and whether they are independent of the crashes.

### Additional information

Related earlier report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48447

Latest Crashpad metadata: a42a180e-97a6-4a32-8016-2496090a215a_sidecar.json (2026-09-26 23:02:23.769 KST). Previous: 1b43d138-4bd9-4e78-8d76-119584020aff_sidecar.json (22:54:41.001 KST).

Only sidecar metadata was available in the inspected reports directory, not an analyzable native dump. Timestamp correlation does not establish causation. No deliberate crash reproduction, cache deletion or settings reset was performed.

Three user-reported password-save prompt strings: synthetic-reference-writer-00000000001; view-test-0--------------------------------; reference-0--------------------------------. Prompt source and relationship to the crashes remain unconfirmed. Stored credentials and full chat transcripts are excluded.

items.title: Linux: system-wide stalls and Ghostty display-flush exit during multi-session CLI use

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

Intermittent, long freezes affect the entire Linux desktop while multiple Codex CLI sessions are open. The user noticed them after the recent update that enabled fullscreen transcripts by default. The latest observed incident ended with Ghostty exiting after a GDK display-flush error.

This report supplies host measurements, not a confirmed Codex root cause. There was substantial I/O and memory pressure, multiple Codex versions were running, and other applications were present. No controlled fullscreen-versus-scrollback comparison has been performed.

## Codex version and process inventory

The installed CLI reports **0.157.1**. A read-only process inventory approximately one hour after the incident found **22 interactive Codex CLI processes and two app-server processes**:

| Executable version | Interactive CLI processes | App-server processes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0.154.0 | 10 | 0 |
| 0.155.1 | 4 | 0 |
| 0.156.1 | 2 | 0 |
| 0.157.0 | 1 | 0 |
| 0.157.1 | 5 | 2 |

Versions were checked against the executables of the running processes, rather than assuming that every session used the version currently on PATH. Of these 24 processes, 23 started before the incident and one afterward. This is a **post-incident snapshot of surviving processes**, not a complete process census at the moment of the freeze. The interactive processes were not necessarily all actively generating responses.

At that snapshot, the 24 native Codex processes together had approximately **2.5 GiB RSS and 2.2 GiB swapped memory**. These totals exclude their non-Codex child processes; RSS also does not deduplicate shared mappings.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, x86-64; kernel 7.0.0-30-generic.
- GNOME on Wayland; 20 logical CPUs; approximately 37.6 GiB RAM.
- 32 GiB configured swap: 16 GiB disk swap plus 16 GiB zram. Zram also consumes physical RAM for compressed pages.
- Ghostty: locally built development revision `94d775fef`, with version string `1.3.2-fix-gtk-stale-mouse-state-+94d775fef`. This is the desktop application's actual executable, not the separate 1.3.1 binary on PATH.
- Ghostty uses its GTK/OpenGL frontend; GTK runtime 4.22.4.
- Intel Iris Xe integrated graphics plus NVIDIA RTX 3050 Mobile; NVIDIA driver 595.84.
- Long-lived detached terminal sessions; the Ghostty service had been running for about 12 days.
- Subscription and per-session model selection are omitted; no particular model has been isolated as a trigger.

## Observed behavior and evidence

The most recent incident was on **2026-09-26, around 12:30–12:33 UTC**. The desktop became broadly unresponsive, affecting applications beyond Ghostty. The user recalls the terminal being idle or is unsure of its exact activity; a scroll, resize, or streaming-output trigger has not been established.

### Ghostty exit

Sanitized journal excerpts:

```text
12:30:50 systemd-journald: Under memory pressure, flushing caches.
12:31:02 systemd-journald: Under memory pressure, flushing caches.
12:31:33 ghostty: info(glib): MESSAGE: Gdk: Error flushing display: Resource temporarily unavailable
12:31:33 systemd: app-com.mitchellh.ghostty.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
12:31:33 systemd: app-com.mitchellh.ghostty.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
12:33:22 systemd: user.slice: The kernel OOM killer killed some processes in this unit.
12:33:22 systemd: user-<redacted>.slice: The kernel OOM killer killed some processes in this unit.
```

Ghostty's recorded termination was **exit status 1**, not a recorded SIGKILL or segmentation fault. Systemd reported OOM activity in the surrounding user slice afterward, but the retained kernel journal does not identify an OOM victim during this incident. Therefore this report does **not** claim that the OOM killer killed Ghostty.

The terminated Ghostty service reported a **2.4 GiB memory peak and 5.3 GiB swap peak over its approximately 12-day lifetime**. These are independent lifetime peaks for the service cgroup, not simultaneous measurements at the freeze, and do not by themselves establish a leak.

### Historical host metrics

Existing sysstat recordings provide roughly ten-minute samples. Times below are UTC:

| Sample time | 1-minute load | Blocked tasks | Swap used | CPU iowait over preceding interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12:00:14 | 1.69 | 49 | 83.64% | 66.96% |
| 12:10:05 | 0.90 | 50 | 83.94% | 77.67% |
| 12:20:09 | 2.68 | 50 | 84.48% | 73.36% |
| 12:30:07 | 225.92 | 264 | 91.48% | 76.21% |
| 12:40:29 | 2.12 | 0 | 59.42% | 22.02% |

At 12:30:07, I/O PSI `some avg60` was **97.32%**, and `full avg60` was **75.40%**. Memory PSI `some avg60` was **8.27%**, and `full avg60` was **6.69%**. Estimated available RAM at that sample was still about **14.1 GiB**; high swap occupancy alone must not be read as proof of global RAM exhaustion.

The NVMe device averaged approximately **377 MiB/s reads** in the interval ending 12:30:07, with an average queue size of **93.72**. These are interval averages, not instantaneous measurements. The records show severe host I/O stalls, but do not identify the process responsible for the reads or the underlying cause.

Earlier that evening, the 10:50:09 UTC sample already showed a 1-minute load of **553.66**, **580 blocked tasks**, and **95.60% swap occupancy**. This was not solely a brief event coinciding with Ghostty's exit.

### Other relevant observations and limitations

- No GPU-hang/reset or NVMe I/O-error message was found in the retained kernel journal for 12:25–12:34 UTC. The NVIDIA driver logged an allocation failure earlier, at 10:55:19 UTC; its relationship to this incident is unknown.
- Other desktop applications exited in the following two minutes. Their reasons for exiting have not been established.
- Post-incident storage inspection found the home filesystem 96% full, with about 14.4 GiB available. `/tmp` was a memory-backed filesystem holding about 15 GiB of files. These are possible background resource contributors, not measurements of their precise use during the freeze or evidence that Codex created them.
- Other applications and development workloads were present. No historical per-process I/O or memory series is available to attribute the stall.
- A full `codex doctor` database-integrity pass has not been run as part of this report. The evidence above came from existing journal/sysstat records and lightweight process inspection.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

No reliable minimal reproducer yet. The observed pattern is intermittent machine-wide freezes during long-lived, multi-session Codex use, noticed after the fullscreen-default update. The exact activity of individual sessions at the latest freeze is unknown.

Expected: interactive Codex and the desktop remain responsive; terminal rendering does not cause unbounded resource pressure or a terminal display-connection failure.

Switching the affected 0.157.x sessions to the older scrollback mode via `/tui` is a proposed isolation test, **not a tested fix for this case**. The simultaneous introduction of automatic background-server startup in 0.157.0 is another reason not to attribute the timing to the renderer alone.

## Related reports

- #48233: 0.157.0 selection latency with Ghostty/Linux over SSH; an OpenAI contributor recommends `/tui`, and the reporter confirms it helps. This describes selection latency, rather than the host-wide stalls and terminal exit observed here.
- #48434: 0.157.1 fullscreen wheel-input/render backlog, measured on Windows.
- #37545: an older Ubuntu whole-desktop freeze report on 0.146.1/0.147.0. Its reporter later said a clean reinstall resolved it; it predates the fullscreen-default change.

## Codex App version

macOS controlling app: 26.924.22138. Linux execution host app: 26.917.71314.

## Subscription

ChatGPT Pro.

## Platform

macOS: Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm. Execution host: Linux desktop app, connected through Codex's remote connection feature.

## Issue

An existing task receives and completes a new message on the Linux host. The Linux app reports the task as unread, but the connected macOS app does not show its blue unread dot. The macOS sidebar can show blue dots for other tasks, so the indicator is available in that UI. Reopening the macOS app, reopening the panel, and checking that notifications are set to push do not restore the missing dot. This makes completed background work hard to discover without opening tasks individually.

## Reproduction

1. Connect the macOS Codex app to a Linux Codex desktop app using the built-in remote connection feature, signed in to the same ChatGPT account.
2. Pick an existing task that appears in the Mac sidebar but is not open. Before the test, both clients report it as not unread.
3. Send that task one ordinary message using the Codex app's native inter-task messaging tool. Wait for the recipient turn to complete and produce a final response.
4. Without opening the recipient task on the Mac, compare its unread status on both clients and the Mac sidebar. Then reopen the Mac app and panel.

In one controlled test on 2026-09-26, the recipient completed at 09:24:12 UTC. The Linux app's `list_threads` returned `isUnread: true`, and its persisted read state included the task. The Mac's persisted read state did not include the task before the test, just after completion, eight minutes later, or after the app was reopened. The Mac sidebar showed no unread dot for that task, while another task did have a blue dot. The user independently confirmed the missing indicator.

## Expected

A completed turn that is unread on the execution host should become visibly unread on connected desktop clients, including when the task was not loaded there at completion. Reconnect or reopening should recover the unread state from durable activity/read information. Opening the task should then clear it according to the normal read behavior.

## Additional diagnostic evidence

The recipient turn finished successfully, so this is not a delivery or execution failure. The Mac and Linux read-state stores have the same account identity and execution-host scope, but the unread membership did not propagate to the Mac. In the inspected macOS build, the `turn/completed` handler skips conversations that are not live in that renderer, and sidebar unread presentation depends on client-local saved state. This is a plausible failure path, not proof that this particular completion event was received and dropped. A missed subscription/event versus an ignored event remains unresolved. Please check completion delivery for unloaded remote threads and durable unread reconciliation on reconnect/listing.

There is a separate phone notification concern, but this controlled test did not measure phone in-app unread or push, so it is not claimed as part of this reproduction. I can provide redacted timestamps and diagnostic captures privately if maintainers need them.

Related but different: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/20930 concerns desktop completion banners. This report is about the missing unread membership and sidebar dot for a completed remote task, even after reopening the app.

ChatGPT pro 5x

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11, x86_64 Codex Desktop with Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2

### What issue are you seeing?

## Additional finding — Windows-native execution fails with ERROR_DIRECTORY (267)

I also switched the Codex execution environment from WSL to native Windows.

The failure changes.

Instead of the WSL permission-profile serialization panic, native Windows execution reports:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess {
  message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process:
  CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267\")"
}
```

Windows error 267 corresponds to:

```text
ERROR_DIRECTORY
The directory name is invalid.
```

This may be related to the same Windows/WSL path-state problem.

The session/project context previously reported its working directory as:

```text
/mnt/d/
```

which is valid in WSL but is not a valid native Windows working-directory representation.

The corresponding native Windows path would be:

```text
D:\
```

or, for the project:

```text
D:\The_Ark
```

This suggests there may be two manifestations of the same path migration/normalization problem:

### WSL execution

```text
permission profile
→ Windows/WSL path normalization
→ non-lossless PathUri/permission serialization
→ panic before tool startup
```

Observed error:

```text
failed to serialize permission profile:
permission path cannot be represented losslessly
```

### Native Windows execution

```text
stored/session working directory remains WSL-style
→ /mnt/d/
→ passed to CreateProcessWithLogonW
→ ERROR_DIRECTORY (267)
```

Observed error:

```text
CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267
```

Please verify that switching execution environments canonicalizes:

- workspace root;
- working directory;
- allowed paths;
- permission-profile paths;

between Windows and WSL representations rather than reusing the previous environment's path representation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex Desktop on Windows 11.

2. Configure Codex to use Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 as the execution environment.

3. Open or create a project on the D: drive. In my case the workspace is on:
   D:\The_Ark

   The corresponding WSL path is:
   /mnt/d/The_Ark

4. Start a completely new Codex chat/project. The issue is not limited to an older migrated conversation.

5. Ask Codex to execute even a trivial command that does not require project filesystem access, for example:

   printf "CODEX_TOOL_OK\n"

6. The tool never starts. Codex fails before shell execution with:

   failed to serialize permission profile:
   permission path cannot be represented losslessly

   A more detailed occurrence was:

   Fatal error: tool task failed to receive:
   JoinError::Panic(..., "failed to serialize permission profile: permission path cannot be represented losslessly", ...)

7. The same error occurs for pwd and for paths such as:
   /
   /tmp
   /mnt
   /mnt/d
   /mnt/d/
   /mnt/d/The_Ark

8. Regranting project/D: drive permissions does not resolve the issue.

9. Creating a completely new project and completely new chat also does not resolve it.

10. If I switch Codex from WSL execution to native Windows execution, the failure changes to:

    CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267

   So both execution environments currently fail, but with different path-related errors.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should successfully initialize the local tool/sandbox environment and execute commands.

For example:

printf "CODEX_TOOL_OK\n"

should return:

CODEX_TOOL_OK

and:

pwd

should execute normally.

When using WSL2, Codex should consistently canonicalize Windows and WSL workspace/permission paths.

Equivalent drive-root representations such as:

D:\
/mnt/d
/mnt/d/

should not cause the permission profile serializer to panic because of a lossless round-trip mismatch.

When switching to native Windows execution, Codex should use a valid Windows working directory such as:

D:\The_Ark

rather than retaining a WSL-style working directory such as:

/mnt/d/The_Ark

A malformed or non-lossless permission entry should also ideally produce a recoverable diagnostic identifying the problematic entry instead of preventing every local tool from starting.

### Additional information

This started after Codex Desktop was updated. The PC had been off/restarted after approximately one week, and the same project/filesystem had worked normally with Codex before the update.

Environment:

Codex Desktop: 26.924.22138
Build: 11645
Windows package: 26.924.2738.0
Codex runtime: 0.158.0-alpha.2.1
OS: Windows 11 x86_64
Linux environment: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2
Sandbox: workspace-write
Permission profile: managed/restricted
Review mode: auto_review

Hardware:
AMD Ryzen 9 5950X
96 GB RAM
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
Samsung 990 PRO 2 TB workspace drive (D:)

A read-only diagnostic was able to inspect the visible permission profile before normal tool execution.

It contained both:

/mnt/d
/mnt/d/

A normal wslpath string round-trip showed:

/mnt/d
→ D:\
→ /mnt/d/

so the original /mnt/d string is not returned exactly, whereas /mnt/d/ round-trips normally.

This does not prove that this is the exact entry rejected by Codex's internal PathUri serializer, because the failing internal entry is not exposed in the error message. However, it appears relevant to the "cannot be represented losslessly" error.

The diagnostic also found both Windows and WSL project registrations in local Codex configuration and evidence of previous project migration state. However, the bug also reproduces in a completely new project and new chat.

Importantly, even a filesystem-independent printf command fails before execution. Therefore there is currently no evidence that the underlying NTFS filesystem, D: drive permissions, Git repository, or project files are causing the failure.

Native Windows execution produces a second potentially related symptom:

CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267

Windows error 267 is ERROR_DIRECTORY ("The directory name is invalid").

This may indicate that WSL-style and Windows-style working-directory/path state is not being consistently converted when switching execution environments.

No project files, Git history, databases, NTFS permissions, WSL mounts, or system settings were modified during diagnosis.

It would be very useful if the permission serialization error logged:
- the failing permission entry index;
- original path;
- normalized/internal PathUri;
- round-trip result.

That would make this regression much easier to diagnose.
