items.body:
## What issue are you seeing?

On Windows, ChatGPT Remote control through `codex-cli` does not work. When the user enables remote pairing, the local daemon either fails to start or exits immediately, no pairing code is produced, and the connection status remains `disconnected`.

The failure is local to the Windows host — there is no network or auth problem involved; it reproduces with a freshly installed standalone `codex.exe` on Windows 10/11 without any ChatGPT client interaction beyond enabling the feature.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install `codex-cli` standalone managed on Windows 10/11 (binary resolves to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\…\bin\codex.exe`).
2. In the ChatGPT client, enable Remote control for the Windows device.
3. Observe: the daemon does not reach `status=connected`. No pairing code is emitted. Local log shows the daemon exiting before the listener becomes ready.

The failure is rooted in Unix-only assumptions in `codex-cli` / `codex-app-server-daemon`:

- Daemon lifecycle uses POSIX `fork` + `setsid` and signal handlers that have no Win32 equivalent.
- The PID/lock file relies on `flock`-style semantics; on Windows the lock is missing or behaves differently, so the daemon either refuses to start (stale PID) or fails to acquire exclusivity.
- PID reuse is real on Windows (PIDs cycle faster than on Linux). Without validating PID via process start time, a recycled PID can be mistaken for a live previous instance.
- The standalone managed binary path is resolved as if the layout matched Unix, and does not point at `current/bin/codex.exe` on Windows.

## What is the expected behavior?

- The daemon starts in detached mode using equivalent Win32 process primitives, so it survives the spawning shell exit.
- Process exclusivity is enforced through a Win32 lock (`LockFileEx`) plus PID + process start time, so PID reuse cannot fool the daemon into thinking another instance is live.
- The standalone managed binary resolves to `current/bin/codex.exe` on Windows.
- The control socket stays private (no public listener).
- Auto-update stays disabled on Windows until a supported Windows installer workflow is available.
- A valid pairing code is emitted and the daemon reaches `status=connected`.

## Additional information

**Root-cause analysis (high level):** the daemon lifecycle module is Unix-shaped end-to-end. Porting it to Windows requires (a) a Win32 detached-process spawn path, (b) Win32 exclusive locking with PID+start-time identity, (c) correct standalone binary resolution, (d) keeping auto-update disabled until installer support exists.

**Working reference implementation:** I maintain a personal fork with the fix already merged into `main`, plus Windows-focused tests for PID reuse and lock exclusivity. It is offered as reference only — I understand openai/codex does not accept external PRs, so I am not opening one.

- Fork: https://github.com/antoniooreany/codex-fork
- Merged change: https://github.com/antoniooreany/codex-fork/pull/1
- Branch: `fix/windows-remote-control-daemon` (merged into fork's `main`)

**Validation on Windows 11 (in the fork):**

- `just test -p codex-app-server-daemon` — 7 passed
- `just test -p codex-cli --bin codex` — 243 passed
- `cargo fmt -p codex-app-server-daemon -- --check` — passed
- `cargo build -p codex-cli` — passed (debug)
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Runtime: daemon reached `status=connected` and emitted a pairing code

**Scope note:** I am reporting this as a bug per the project's contribution guidelines, with RCA and a reference fix, rather than opening a PR.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.2738.0

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

After recent Codex Desktop updates on Windows, authentication started failing with:

`token_exchange_failed: error sending request for url (https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token)`

I performed extensive troubleshooting and isolated the failure to an interoperability issue between newly created Codex runtime executables and Kaspersky Premium Application Control / Intrusion Prevention.

## Affected versions

Current affected installation:

- Codex Desktop: `26.924.2738.0`
- Runtime: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`
- Runtime path: `C:\Users\luiza\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\bin\faa963e871dd422c\codex.exe`

Previous installation observed during troubleshooting:

- Codex Desktop: `26.924.1866.0`
- Runtime: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2`

Possibly related to #47343, but this report includes an isolated root cause and a confirmed workaround.

## What happens

Codex updates create a new runtime directory/hash and therefore a new `codex.exe`.

After the update to `26.924.2738.0`, Kaspersky Premium detected the newly created runtime executable as a new application.

Although the executable has a valid digital signature from `OpenAI OpCo, LLC`, Kaspersky initially classified it as:

- Trust group: **Low Restricted**
- Digital signature: `OpenAI OpCo, LLC`
- Certificate status: **Trusted (not approved)**

Kaspersky then assigned restrictive/denied network rules to that new `codex.exe`.

The result was:

`Codex update -> new codex.exe/runtime path -> Kaspersky classifies it as Low Restricted -> outbound network access is restricted -> Codex reports token_exchange_failed`

## Causal confirmation / workaround

I changed ONLY the Kaspersky network permissions for the newly created affected `codex.exe` from restricted/denied to **Allow** for Trusted, Local, and Public networks.

I did NOT:

- reboot Windows;
- reinstall or repair Codex;
- disable Kaspersky;
- change DNS;
- change IPv4/IPv6 settings;
- modify certificates;
- change proxy settings;
- change my OpenAI account.

Immediately after changing only those Kaspersky network permissions to Allow, Codex authentication succeeded.

I then moved that executable from Kaspersky's **Low Restricted** group to **Trusted**, where the other existing OpenAI/Codex components are located.

## Important Kaspersky configuration

Kaspersky Premium was already configured with:

- **Trust digitally signed applications: Enabled**
- **Load rules for applications from Kaspersky Security Network (KSN): Enabled**
- Applications not assigned to another group default to **Low Restricted**

Kaspersky also recognizes `OpenAI OpCo, LLC` as the vendor for existing Codex components and has an `OPENAI OPCO` grouping containing trusted Codex executables.

This suggests that very newly released Codex runtime binaries may temporarily be treated as unknown/Low Restricted before reputation information is available, despite being validly signed by OpenAI.

Because Codex runtime updates create new executable paths/hashes, this can potentially recur after future updates.

## Network diagnostics already performed

Before isolating the Kaspersky rule, I verified:

- DNS resolution for `auth.openai.com`: working
- TCP 443: working
- HTTPS/TLS: working
- Direct POST to `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token`: reaches OpenAI and receives the expected HTTP response
- Same POST test over IPv4: working
- Same POST test over IPv6: working
- WinHTTP proxy: none
- `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`: not configured
- Git proxy: none
- Codex `config.toml`: no custom proxy/TLS/CA configuration
- Authenticode signature of affected `codex.exe`: Valid, signed by `OpenAI OpCo, LLC`
- MSIX package status: `Ok`

The issue was also reproducible by invoking the affected `codex.exe` runtime directly.

## Suggested investigation

It may be useful for OpenAI to:

1. Coordinate with Kaspersky/KSN so newly released, validly signed `OpenAI OpCo, LLC` Codex binaries receive appropriate reputation/trust immediately.
2. Investigate whether the runtime/update packaging can reduce repeated classification as a completely new unknown application by endpoint security products.
3. Improve the error surfaced by Codex. `token_exchange_failed: error sending request` hides the underlying application-level network restriction and makes diagnosis difficult.
4. Consider detecting this condition and recommending that users inspect endpoint-security Application Control / network rules.

I have screenshots documenting the affected runtime path, OpenAI digital signature, Low Restricted classification, denied network rules, the changed Allow rules, Kaspersky configuration, and successful Codex operation after the single network-rule change.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install/run Codex Desktop on Windows with Kaspersky Premium Intrusion Prevention / Application Control enabled.

2. Have Kaspersky configured normally with:
   - "Trust digitally signed applications" enabled.
   - Kaspersky Security Network (KSN) application rules enabled.
   - Unclassified applications defaulting to "Low Restricted".

3. Update Codex Desktop to a build that installs a newly created runtime executable under a new hash-named directory.

   In my reproduced case:

   - Codex Desktop: `26.924.2738.0`
   - Runtime: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`
   - New runtime path:
     `C:\Users\luiza\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\bin\faa963e871dd422c\codex.exe`

4. Kaspersky detects this newly created `codex.exe` as a new application. Despite its valid `OpenAI OpCo, LLC` digital signature, it is initially placed in the **Low Restricted** trust group.

5. Kaspersky assigns restrictive/denied network rules to the new executable for Trusted, Local, and Public networks.

6. Open Codex Desktop and choose "Continue to sign in".

7. Complete the ChatGPT authorization flow in the browser.

8. The browser successfully returns to the local Codex callback, but the token exchange fails:

   `token_exchange_failed: error sending request for url (https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token)`

9. The same failure can be reproduced directly with the affected runtime:

   `codex.exe login`

10. In Kaspersky, change ONLY the network rules for this newly created `codex.exe` from restricted/denied to **Allow** for Trusted, Local, and Public networks.

11. Retry the normal Codex authentication flow.

### Result

Authentication succeeds immediately.

No reboot, Codex reinstall/repair, Kaspersky shutdown, DNS change, proxy change, certificate change, IPv4/IPv6 change, or OpenAI account change is required.

Moving the same executable from Kaspersky's **Low Restricted** trust group to **Trusted** also places it alongside the other existing OpenAI/Codex components.

### Additional observation

Codex runtime updates use new hash-named directories/executable identities. Therefore the problem may recur when a future update creates another new runtime that Kaspersky/KSN has not yet established reputation for.

### What is the expected behavior?

After a Codex Desktop update, newly installed runtime components that are validly signed by `OpenAI OpCo, LLC` should be able to communicate with the required OpenAI services without authentication unexpectedly breaking.

Ideally:

1. Newly released Codex executables should be recognized promptly by major endpoint-security/reputation systems such as Kaspersky/KSN.

2. A routine Codex update should not result in a newly created runtime being treated as an unknown/Low Restricted application with outbound network access denied.

3. If endpoint-security software blocks the Codex runtime, Codex should surface a diagnostic error that identifies an outbound connectivity/application-control problem rather than only:

   `token_exchange_failed: error sending request`

4. The error message should ideally recommend checking endpoint-security Application Control / network rules when the OAuth endpoint is reachable from the system but inaccessible to the Codex process.

5. Users should not need to manually reclassify or authorize a newly created `codex.exe` after each runtime update.

### Additional information

## Related issue

This may be related to #47343 (`ChatGPT Desktop Windows: token_exchange_failed when exchanging OAuth token`).

The important difference in this report is that I was able to isolate a specific cause and verify it experimentally: Kaspersky Application Control / Intrusion Prevention classified the newly created Codex runtime as **Low Restricted** and applied restrictive network rules. Changing only those rules to **Allow** immediately restored authentication.

This may also explain why disabling Kaspersky Firewall, Web Antivirus, or HTTPS inspection alone may not resolve similar reports: the restriction can exist at the per-application trust/network-rule level.

## Runtime update behavior observed

Before the latest update:

- Desktop: `26.924.1866.0`
- Runtime: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2`
- Runtime directory: `d23520d1e41bfb24`

After the update:

- Desktop: `26.924.2738.0`
- Runtime: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`
- Runtime directory: `faa963e871dd422c`

The update therefore created a new executable identity/path that was independently evaluated by Kaspersky.

## Kaspersky observations

The affected executable showed:

- Vendor/signature: `OpenAI OpCo, LLC`
- Trust group: `Low Restricted`
- Certificate status: `Trusted (not approved)`
- Network rules: restricted/denied
- Kaspersky indicated that the application had appeared very recently.

Existing Codex/OpenAI components were already present under Kaspersky's **Trusted** group, including an `OPENAI OPCO` vendor grouping.

After confirming the network-rule workaround, I manually moved the affected runtime from **Low Restricted** to **Trusted**.

## Why I believe this is worth investigating on the Codex side

Even if the initial classification originates from Kaspersky/KSN, Codex currently surfaces the resulting failure only as:

`token_exchange_failed: error sending request`

That makes this condition appear to be an OpenAI OAuth/server/network problem and makes the actual application-level block very difficult to identify.

There may therefore be opportunities both to coordinate reputation/signing behavior with Kaspersky and to improve Codex's own connectivity diagnostics.

OpenAI Support was contacted first and recommended filing this reproducible Codex Desktop issue here with the exact Kaspersky rule change/workaround documented.

2. Clicking either tab has no effect—the category cannot be switched.
3. Due to `gap-0` in `browse` tab variant styles, both active capsule pills touch with 0px spacing, appearing visually glued together.
4. Switching the app language back to English immediately fixes the issue (tabs become `Personal` and `System`, can be toggled cleanly).

Screenshot:
![Skills scope tabs collision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Michael-IT001/codex-bluepaper/main/assets/codex_skills_scope_tabs_collision.png)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Set Codex UI / system language to Simplified Chinese (`zh-CN`).
2. Open Codex Desktop App and navigate to the Skills page (`/skills`).
3. Ensure both user-installed skills and system skills are present so multiple scope categories exist.
4. Observe the scope category filter pills under the header: both `个人` and `系统` are highlighted simultaneously.
5. Attempt to click `系统` (or `个人`): the selection does not change and the view does not filter.
6. Switch app language to English: notice `Personal` and `System` tabs now work correctly.

### What is the expected behavior?

Each scope category tab should have a unique identifier regardless of the UI language. Only the actively selected tab should have the `selected` styling, and clicking another tab should switch the view to filter that category.

### Additional information (Root Cause Analysis & Code Evidence)

Decompiling the webview bundle reveals the root cause in `skills-page-*.js`:

#### 1. Regex Wipes Out Non-ASCII Characters in Slug Generator
```javascript
function At({ intl: e, roots: t, skillEntries: n }) {
  let r = new Map();
  for (let i of n) {
    let n = ze({ skill: i.skill, roots: t, intl: e }), // Localized scope label: "个人" or "系统"
      a = r.get(n);
    if (a == null) {
      r.set(n, {
        id: `skills-installed-${jt(n)}`, // <--- BUG: jt(n) produces collision
        title: n,
        skillEntries: [i],
      });
      continue;
    }
    a.skillEntries.push(i);
  }
  return Array.from(r.values());
}

function jt(e) {
  return e
    .trim()
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, `-`); // <--- Strips ALL non-ASCII/CJK characters!
}
```

#### 2. The Resulting Collision
- In English:
  - `"Personal"` -> `jt("Personal")` -> `"personal"` -> ID: `skills-installed-personal`
  - `"System"` -> `jt("System")` -> `"system"` -> ID: `skills-installed-system`
  (Unique IDs, works as expected)

- In Chinese (`zh-CN`):
  - `"个人"` contains no characters in `[a-z0-9]`. The entire string matches `[^a-z0-9]+` and is replaced by `"-"`.
    -> ID: `skills-installed--`
  - `"系统"` also contains no `[a-z0-9]` characters.
    -> ID: `skills-installed--`

Both categories are assigned the exact same ID (`skills-installed--`).

#### 3. Consequence in the Tabs Component (`JZe` in `app-primary-*.js`)
- `tabs: [{ key: 'skills-installed--', name: '个人' }, { key: 'skills-installed--', name: '系统' }]`
- `isTabSelected = (tab.key === selectedKey)` evaluates to `true` for **both** tabs.
- Both tabs receive `selectedClassName` (`bg-primary-ghost-hover text-default`), causing both to appear lit up.
- Clicking either tab triggers `if (!isTabSelected) { onSelect(tab.key) }`, which is short-circuited because `isTabSelected` is already true.

#### Suggested Fix
Do not slugify the localized label `n` with an ASCII-only regex to build the section `id`. Instead, use the canonical skill scope key (`i.skill.scope`, e.g. `'user'`, `'system'`, `'repo'`, `'admin'`) to derive the stable ID:
```javascript
// Suggested:
id: `skills-installed-${i.skill.scope || jt(n)}`
```
or use a slugifier that preserves Unicode letters (e.g. `\p{L}` / encodeURIComponent).

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### Which model were you using?

_No response_

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Terminal + Powershell

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

On Windows, a batch of visible console windows flashes for `git.exe` / `pwsh.exe` (and other helper) child processes:

- several `git.exe` windows on every new session, and again on every turn;
- `pwsh.exe` windows for shell/exec child processes.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, run `codex` interactively (e.g. in Windows Terminal) on a project inside a git repository (default config, no `--no-daemon`).
2. Start a new thread and send a turn.
3. Observe console windows flashing for `git.exe` (session start + every turn) and `pwsh.exe` (shell/exec helpers).

Workaround that confirms the diagnosis: `codex --no-daemon` runs the session embedded in the TUI process (console attached), and the flashing stops.


### What is the expected behavior?

No visible console windows. Helper subprocesses spawned by the console-less daemon backend should either inherit a hidden console or be created with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`.


### Additional information

Source analysis at tag `rust-v0.157.1`:

Why the spawning process has no console:
- `codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs:941-944` — `daemon_auto_start` is enabled by default.
- `codex-rs/tui/src/startup_orchestration.rs:494-544` — TUI auto-starts the shared daemon and targets `AppServerTarget::LocalDaemon` (session runs in the daemon's app-server backend, not in the TUI).
- `codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/backend/pid_start.rs:209` — backend spawn uses `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` → no console. `spawn_without_inheriting_stdio` (`backend/windows.rs:56+`) only clears stdio handle inheritance and adds no window suppression.

Unsuppressed child spawns from that console-less backend:
- `git.exe` (dominant source): `codex-rs/git-utils/src/git_process.rs:47-63` goes through `JobObject::spawn_contained`, and `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/job.rs:125-127` only sets `CREATE_SUSPENDED` (no `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`); the fallback path resets `creation_flags(0)`. Volume: new session → `codex-rs/rollout/src/recorder.rs:1977-1978` → `collect_git_info` (`git-utils/src/info.rs:66-82`) = 4 spawns; every turn → `codex-rs/core/src/turn_metadata.rs:547-551` = 3 more (plus a possible fsmonitor probe). Direct `Command::new("git")` sites in `git-utils` (apply.rs / baseline.rs / branch.rs / operations.rs) share the gap.
- `pwsh.exe` / shell helpers: `codex-rs/exec-server/src/fs_sandbox.rs:516`, `codex-rs/exec-server/src/shell_snapshot.rs:287`, `codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/unified_exec/backends/legacy.rs:118` (`ConsoleMode::Inherit`, mapped to flags 0 in `process.rs:109-113`; default `WindowsSandboxLevel::Disabled` takes this path), `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs:233-245`, `codex-rs/hooks/src/legacy_notify.rs:53-66`, `codex-rs/cli/src/desktop_app/windows.rs:34-56`.
- The codebase already sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` correctly elsewhere (e.g. `bin/command_runner/win.rs:351`, `rmcp-client/src/stdio_server_launcher.rs:297`), so this looks like an omission.
- Checked against current `main` (e72da2b5, 2026-09-26): `git_process.rs`, `job.rs`, `legacy.rs`, `pid_start.rs` are unchanged vs 0.157.1 — upgrading does not fix this.

Suggested fix:
1. Minimal: in `codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/backend/pid_start.rs:209`, replace `DETACHED_PROCESS` with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (keeps the backend detached from the launching terminal and breakaway-safe, but gives it a hidden console that children inherit — removes the flashing for all daemon-managed backends in one line).
2. Robust: also set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` at the individual spawn sites above (git_process / job.rs, unified_exec legacy backend + `(None, NoWindow)` mapping in `process.rs:109-113`, exec-server spawns, hooks, desktop_app powershell) so any console-less parent is covered.

- 記録上のpolicy表示はworkspace-write／granular。sandbox_approval・rules・skill_approvalは自動拒否、request_permissions・mcp_elicitationsは確認可能でした。この表示だけで実効設定の供給元や起動判定の内部条件を特定したとはしていません。
- 正確なアプリ/core版、実効policyの供給層・管理主体は不明です。今回、版確認・設定採取・再実行はしていません。

## P03 直接引用：外側ツールの拒否本文
以下は既存記録の2提出で同一だった返却本文を1回だけ転記したものです。curlやHTTPS相手からの出力ではありません。前後のラベルや記録全体を再現した合成ログではありません。

~~~text
Script error:
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"approval required by policy, but AskForApproval::Granular.sandbox_approval is false\")" }
~~~

## P04 意図した操作の編集要約（実施・制御の有効性は未確認）
対象はUbuntu公式の公開.dscに対する通常のHTTPS GET一件でした。Windows上のcurlをshellからProcessStartInfo経由で開始する記述です。
意図した記述にはTLS／proxy証明書検証有効、HTTPS限定、自動redirect・retryなし、接続10秒・転送15秒、本文32,768 bytes・stderr8,192 bytes等のpayload境界がありました。ただしshell起動前拒否のため、これらの制御が有効に働いたことを実測したわけではありません。payload境界はnative／TLS／RSS込みの全保持上界ではありません。
元の実行可能な呼出し全文、ローカルpath、内部出力マーカー、詳細capture／停止処理は、この候補には含めていません。

## P05 求める判断
1. この種の起動前拒否について、sandbox承認を必要と判定する規則・条件を、開示可能な範囲で説明できますか。今回の固有原因をこの編集要約だけで特定できない場合は、その限界を区別してください。

HTTP status、対象GETの所要時間、DNS／TCP／TLS／証明書検証結果、client exit codeは取得されていません。起動前拒否をネットワークやTLS障害の原因特定とは扱いません。

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.1866.0

Also reproduced on 26.903.8094.0.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

When multiple `fire_confetti` tool calls are dispatched in rapid succession, the Codex App repeatedly shows only a small launch fragment from each burst. Each later invocation resets or removes the preceding visual state, and only the final invocation completes its trajectory.

All 100 invocations return `{"fired":true}`, even though the accepted bursts are not presented completely. The visible output is not one clean coalesced burst or a queue of complete bursts; it is a series of truncated launch fragments followed by one complete final burst.

This was reproduced with paper-only confetti (`{"emojis":[]}`) on 2026-09-26 (Asia/Seoul) using Codex App 26.924.1866.0. The same behavior was previously recorded on 26.903.8094.0.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Enable **Settings → Toys → Confetti cannon**.
2. Open a task in the Windows Codex App.
3. Dispatch 100 `fire_confetti` calls concurrently, each with:
   ```json
   {"emojis":[]}
   ```
4. Observe the animation in the active Codex window.
5. Compare the visual result with the per-call responses.

Observed response summary:

```text
paper_only_calls=100 fired_ack=100 other=0
```

Observed rendering:

- Many calls briefly show particles near the launch edge.
- Intermediate trajectories are visibly reset or removed.
- Only the final call completes normally.
- The result is substantially different from 100 complete bursts, despite all calls reporting success.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should apply and report one explicit policy consistently. For example:

1. Queue accepted bursts and render them completely.
2. Coalesce rapid calls into one coherent burst and report that they were coalesced.
3. Reject or rate-limit excess calls with an explicit status.
4. If only the latest call is retained, report superseded calls instead of returning `fired:true` for every invocation.

The current combination of partial presentation, supersession, and unconditional success acknowledgement is internally inconsistent.

### Additional information

A 15.7333-second, 570×564, 30 fps H.264 screen recording of the original reproduction is preserved locally.

Recording SHA-256:

```text
E602CD813559046318D41CE96A826046E8F1BB026B8ECE04FA0432A922D5A690
```

Inspection of the packaged frontend in version 26.903.8094.0 suggested the following mechanism:

- Each invocation calls a module-level cleanup callback for the preceding cannon.
- Cleanup removes the previous canvas and clears its batch.
- A new full-window canvas and animation engine are created.
- The handler returns `fired:true` immediately after scheduling and does not wait for presentation or completion.
- Already scheduled animation-frame callbacks were not all explicitly cancelled during cleanup.

That implementation observation is version-specific; the current 26.924.1866.0 reproduction confirms the visible behavior, not that the internal implementation is unchanged.

Potential regression coverage:

- One call: one complete burst.
- 10 sequential calls: defined queue/coalescing behavior without partial resets.
- 10 and 100 concurrent calls: no truncated fragments and truthful per-call statuses.
- Paper-only, default emoji mix, and custom emoji modes.
- Reduced-motion and non-visible-window behavior.

items.title: Linux Desktop regression: Codex hangs on every prompt in 26.924.22138, works after downgrade to 26.901.41600

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.22138-1

### What subscription do you have?

pro x5

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.7-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Description

Codex in the ChatGPT Desktop app hangs indefinitely after submitting any prompt on Linux.

The issue is reproducible even with a completely new Codex conversation and a trivial prompt such as:

`Run pwd`

The conversation enters the running state but never completes. The running task also cannot be stopped normally from the UI.

Regular ChatGPT functionality in the Desktop app continues to work.

I was able to isolate this to a regression in the current Desktop release by performing a clean reinstall and an A/B test with an older Desktop build.

## Environment

- OS: Fedora 44 x86_64
- Broken ChatGPT Desktop version: `26.924.22138-1`
- Working ChatGPT Desktop version: `26.901.41600-1`
- Bundled Codex runtime in the broken build: `0.158.0-alpha.2.1`
- Git: `2.55.0` (`/usr/bin/git`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install ChatGPT Desktop `26.924.22138-1` on Fedora 44.
2. Start the application and sign in.
3. Open Codex.
4. Create a new conversation.
5. Send `Run pwd`.
6. The conversation remains running indefinitely.

The same behavior occurs across different projects.

## A/B test

I completely removed the Desktop application and local Codex/Desktop state, including Codex configuration, caches, runtime caches, and local state.

I then performed a clean installation of:

`26.924.22138-1`

The problem was still reproducible immediately, before restoring MCP servers, plugins, previous Codex configuration, or standalone Codex CLI.

I then removed that version and installed the older RPM:

`26.901.41600-1`

using the same machine, Fedora installation, network, and account.

Codex immediately started working normally again.

So:

- `26.924.22138-1` → Codex hangs
- `26.901.41600-1` → Codex works

## Bundled Codex runtime test

The Codex runtime bundled with the broken `26.924.22138` Desktop installation itself works correctly when executed outside the Desktop UI.

Running:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex --version`

returned:

`codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`

And:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Run pwd"`

successfully executed `/bin/bash -lc pwd` and returned the working directory immediately.

This suggests that the bundled Codex runtime itself is functional and that the regression is likely somewhere in the Linux Desktop ↔ Codex integration.

## Additional diagnostics

On the broken build, the Desktop app-server successfully initialized:

- `Transport start success`
- `initialize_handshake_result ... outcome=success`
- `Codex CLI initialized`
- connection state became `connected`

The logs also contained:

`Failed to load shell env caller=startup detail="Timed out after 5000ms."`

and:

`git fetch failed: Git is unavailable`

`Worktree archive will be retried ... Git is unavailable`

However, Git itself is installed and works normally at `/usr/bin/git`.

A manual login-shell test:

`time /bin/bash -lic 'echo SHELL_OK; command -v git; command -v node; command -v codex; exit'`

completed successfully in approximately 0.6 seconds.

I also tested:

- minimal `~/.codex/config.toml`
- MCP/plugins disabled
- Computer Use disabled
- Desktop RPM reinstall
- standalone Codex CLI update

None of these changed the behavior on `26.924.22138`.

The downgrade to `26.901.41600` immediately resolved the issue.

## Expected behavior

A newly submitted Codex prompt should start and complete normally, as it does on Desktop `26.901.41600`.

## Actual behavior

On Desktop `26.924.22138`, Codex enters the running state indefinitely after submitting a prompt and the task cannot be stopped normally from the UI.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install ChatGPT Desktop `26.924.22138-1` on Fedora 44 x86_64.
2. Launch ChatGPT Desktop and sign in.
3. Open the Codex section.
4. Create a new Codex conversation in any local project.
5. Send a simple prompt such as `Run pwd`.
6. The conversation enters the running state but never completes.
7. Attempting to stop the running task from the UI also does not work.

The issue reproduces across different projects and new conversations.

For comparison, on the exact same machine, account, network, and Fedora installation, downgrading only ChatGPT Desktop to `26.901.41600-1` immediately resolves the issue.

### What is the expected behavior?

Submitting a prompt in Codex should start and complete normally, and the running task should be stoppable from the UI if needed.

The same workflow works correctly on ChatGPT Desktop `26.901.41600-1`.

### Additional information

_No response_

In the macOS ChatGPT desktop app, the Simplified Chinese label for **Open source licenses** in Codex **Settings → General** reads **“打开源许可证”**. It appears beside the description **“捆绑依赖项的第三方声明”** and the **“查看”** button. The natural translation of this noun phrase is **“开源许可证”**.

Read-only inspection of the installed `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` found the following in `webview/assets/zh-CN-1adc76a05252.js`:

```text
settings.openSourceLicenses.rowLabel: 打开源许可证
settings.openSourceLicenses.title: 打开源许可证
```

The English defaults for both IDs are **“Open source licenses”**. The row was observed in the UI by the reporter. The destination page-title value was verified in the installed resource; it was not independently captured from the UI.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the macOS **ChatGPT** desktop app and use **Simplified Chinese (zh-CN)** in the Codex view.
2. Open **Settings → General** (`设置 → 常规`).
3. Find the row with the description **“捆绑依赖项的第三方声明”** and the **“查看”** button.
4. Observe the row label, then select **“查看”** to inspect the destination page title.

The packaged General settings code routes the button from `/settings/general-settings` to `/settings/open-source-licenses`. No session ID, prompt, token limit, or context-window usage is involved; this is a static UI translation.

### What is the expected behavior?

The settings row and destination page title should both say **“开源许可证”**, matching the English default **“Open source licenses”**. The separate **“查看”** action should remain unchanged.

### Additional information

**Installed build:** ChatGPT.app 26.924.22138 (bundle build 11645), bundle ID `com.openai.codex`; macOS 26.6.2 / Apple Silicon.

**Affected packaged resource:** `app.asar/webview/assets/zh-CN-1adc76a05252.js` (2,093,436 bytes; SHA-256 `3e1d624cba5efba65c6a777b4c20e390332ceda9794543a329220827db3ba9ab`). Full `app.asar` SHA-256: `d0ba973179d2f717affd39e012b64a095464a54a51c6bccb7bc6b3d2a1cfba80`. These hashes identify this build; hashed filenames may change in future releases.

**English call sites in the packaged app:** `webview/assets/notifications-settings-4d0e743da3bb.js` defines the row label; `general-settings-e5ae319561ed.js` uses it; `open-source-licenses-page-695070de8f72.js` defines the title. The `zh-CN` bundle also maps `settings.general.groupTitle` to “常规”, confirming the settings path.

**Suggested fix:** Change the source `zh-CN` translations for `settings.openSourceLicenses.rowLabel` and `settings.openSourceLicenses.title` to “开源许可证”, then regenerate the desktop locale assets. Please fix the source entries rather than patching the distributed `app.asar`.

**Verification:** In a fixed build, use zh-CN and check both the General-settings row and the destination title; select “查看” and confirm notices still load. Switch to English and confirm both locations still say “Open source licenses”. Retain the tested version and screenshot or run log.

OpenAI staff previously stated that the desktop app is not open source: https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/16538 . The current contribution guide directs bug reports and root-cause analyses to Issues and says external PRs are not accepted: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/docs/contributing.md .

items.title: 0.157: TUI sessions created through the shared app-server daemon are recorded as `source: vscode` instead of `cli`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.157.1 (also read against the `rust-v0.157.0` source)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6-luna (not model-specific)

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Not terminal-specific

### Codex doctor report

Not included: the behavior follows from the source code below and is not environment-specific. Happy to provide it if needed.

### What issue are you seeing?

Since 0.157, an interactive `codex` TUI session is created by the shared app-server daemon (`codex app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon`), and the thread is recorded with the daemon's session source, `vscode`, instead of `cli`.

`thread/list` results grouped by `source` / `originator` / `cliVersion`:

| source   | originator      | cliVersion   | count |
|----------|-----------------|--------------|-------|
| `cli`    | `codex-tui`     | 0.152–0.156  | 7     |
| `vscode` | `codex-tui`     | 0.157.1      | 15    |
| `vscode` | `Codex Desktop` | 0.155        | 2     |
| `exec`   | `codex_exec`    | 0.150–0.154  | 15    |

So the same terminal UI now produces `source: vscode`, which is indistinguishable from IDE / desktop threads by `source`. The only field that still tells them apart is `originator`.

Where it comes from (tag `rust-v0.157.0`):

- `tui/src/lib.rs` (~L708): the embedded in-process app-server is started with `session_source: "cli"` and `client_name: "codex-tui"`.
- `cli/src/main.rs` (~L1270): the `app-server` subcommand (which the managed daemon runs) always passes `SessionSource::VSCode` to `run_main_with_transport_options`.
- Threads started over the daemon therefore take the daemon's source, not the connecting client's.

Consequences:

- `thread/list` with `sourceKinds: ["cli"]` no longer returns any thread started from the TUI on 0.157.
- `ThreadListParams.originators` cannot select TUI threads either: it is documented as "Supported by hosted backends only; the local app-server rejects a nonempty list".
- The `Thread.source` doc ("Origin of the thread (CLI, VSCode, codex exec, codex app-server, etc.)") no longer describes TUI threads correctly.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. With Codex 0.157.x, run `codex` in a terminal and send one message (the shared daemon starts or is reused).
2. Run `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, `initialize`, then call `thread/list` with `{"sourceKinds": ["cli", "vscode"], "sortKey": "updated_at"}`.
3. The new thread has `"source": "vscode"` and `"originator": "codex-tui"`.
4. Call `thread/list` with `{"sourceKinds": ["cli"]}`: the new thread is missing.

### What is the expected behavior?

A thread started from the TUI is recorded as `source: cli`, as it was up to 0.156, regardless of whether it runs in-process or through the shared daemon. For example the daemon could record the source per connecting client (the TUI already identifies itself as `codex-tui` in `initialize`) instead of using one process-wide source.

Fullscreen interaction can be useful. The concern is silently changing established controls during an update. Terminal users already have platform conventions, settings, and muscle memory; copying a piece of output should not unexpectedly require learning a different interaction model.

### Summary

Between September 24 and September 26, 2026, ChatGPT has been intermittently unstable across the web UI and Android app.

### Observed behavior

- Existing conversations frequently fail to load with messages equivalent to **"Could not load this ChatGPT conversation"** / **"Unable to load this GPT conversation"**.
- On the web UI, refreshing the page a few times can make the same conversation become unavailable even if it loaded previously.
- The failure is intermittent: the same conversation may load normally at one moment and fail shortly afterward.
- On Android, **"Too many requests"** can appear even when no rapid sequence of manual requests is being sent.
- A normal message can then fail with **"Something went wrong"** immediately afterward.
- Image generation may finish, but the generated image / attachment / download control can take a long time to appear in the conversation UI.
- The issue is reproducible even with a single image-generation request; it is not limited to high-concurrency usage.

### Time window

Observed repeatedly from **2026-09-24 through 2026-09-26**.

One concrete Android observation on **2026-09-26 (UTC+8)**:
- 16:31:46 — "Too many requests"
- 16:32:02 — a normal message attempt failed with "Something went wrong"

### Expected behavior

- Existing conversations should load consistently.
- Normal user activity should not trigger intermittent 429-style errors.
- Once image generation is complete, the resulting image/attachment should become available without a long UI delay.
- Refreshing an already accessible conversation should not make it intermittently unloadable.

### Notes

This report intentionally omits conversation contents, account identifiers, conversation IDs, and unrelated user data. No claim is made about the root cause; the timing overlaps with recent UI changes, but that is only an observation, not a confirmed cause.

Account-specific diagnostics can be provided through a private OpenAI Support channel if needed.

The PDF is successfully shown as attached in the prompt composer, but a red error message then appears: Remove and reattach these files to use a different model The message appears even though GPT-6 Astra Ultra was already selected when the PDF was attached. As a result, I cannot submit the prompt with the attached PDF in Work mode. Example prompt: Please explain the contents of the PDF document I attached. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? No code snippet is applicable because this is a ChatGPT Web UI/file attachment issue. Open https://chatgpt.com/ in Google Chrome. Select Work mode. Select GPT-6 Astra Ultra. Attach a PDF file using the prompt composer. Enter a prompt, for example: Please explain the contents of the PDF document I attached. The PDF appears as attached. When a PDF is attached after GPT-6 Astra Ultra has already been selected, the file should remain attached and the prompt should be submitted normally if that model supports PDF attachments. If GPT-6 Astra Ultra does not support PDF attachments in Work mode, the UI should clearly state that the selected model does not support the file type and should prevent the incompatible attachment, rather than accepting the PDF and then displaying a message asking the user to remove and reattach it to use a different model. ### Additional information Environment: Product: ChatGPT Web Mode: Work Model: GPT-6 Astra Ultra Browser: Google Chrome 154.0.8037.58 (Official Build) (64-bit) Operating system: Windows 11 Pro Date observed: 26 September 2026 I have attached a screenshot showing the issue.
